2026-11-06.headline: 从代理模型到拓扑不变量：多尺度预测、无序与边界效应
2026-11-06.overview: 本期论文横跨机器学习代理模型、无序与受限体系、拓扑与量子多体、软物质与活性物质等方向。共同问题在于：当模型或理论从理想条件走向真实条件（留出单元、边界、无序、有限尺寸、非马尔可夫效应）时，预测与判据是否仍然成立。不同路线包括：用可审计的评估与校准暴露代理模型的泛化边界；用规范无关的敏感性图、有效势与精确可解模型刻画无序和受限；用对称性、拓扑不变量与严格界给出定性判据；以及在实验平台上验证理论预言。

themes.title: 代理模型与数据驱动预测的泛化边界
themes.summary: 多篇工作把评估条件本身作为研究对象。SteelBench显示按钢种家族留出时R²由0.859降至0.113、名义90%区间覆盖率降至37.6%，说明随机划分会高估泛化；熔融氯化物腐蚀模型以291组文献静态数据取得交叉验证R²=0.85并给出校准良好的共形区间，但受限于静态测试数据；PolyGPT发现电解质域条件化虽略降Tg误差，却使有效输出唯一性由99.99%降至51.74%、特征包含成功率由94.27%降至31.27%，提示仅凭性质误差评价条件化生成不足；FNO逆向协同设计报告0.6%相对L2误差与约17,000倍加速，但仅为模拟与代理模型结果。

themes.title: 无序、受限与边界如何改写输运与相变
themes.summary: 热流敏感性图在非晶/副晶硅中显示投影热流图与质量/键刚度响应图反相关，软区通过约1–2 meV振动模式混合限制热输运，且约100 K以下残留分量未被软度解释；双曲格点Ising模型中开放边界给出体积型磁化率标度与非平均场指数，wired边界下中心-辅助关联呈平均场磁化指数；纳米孔中4CFPB的Tg由217 K降至208–210 K而脆性约60、超Arrhenius特征保留；MOF-5中波动式声子相干性近乎不变并在500 K贡献约一半本征热导率，而粒子式传播随温度显著减弱。

themes.title: 拓扑判据与对称性：从能带指标到量子存储
themes.summary: 带内例外点受无自旋时间反演保护、成对核化并由带内Z2指数诊断，束缚态尾部在例外点对之间由指数变为振荡；连续介质中旋光型响应在一阶微扰下通常不能打开轴子能隙，而空间色散的交变磁电耦合可以；非阿贝尔对称富集使toric code在任意键错误概率下抵抗非相干电噪声，逻辑错误率随尺寸指数衰减（N≥40为保守界）；二维非手性拓扑序中给出基于Turaev-Viro路径积分的综合征提取与在线解码，并证明局域随机线路级噪声下存在阈值，但未给阈值数值。

themes.title: 强耦合与非马尔可夫动力学修正既有不稳定性图像
themes.summary: 准经典Kadanoff-Baym方程显示计入非马尔可夫效应后，强耦合Migdal-Eliashberg体系不存在马尔可夫量子玻尔兹曼近似预言的不稳定性，中间温区弛豫速率呈线性温度依赖且斜率为普朗克型；一维费米气三体共振处，初始热流衰减最快的共振位置高于积分弛豫时间最短的位置，快初始衰减可与更慢后续弛豫及更大低频热响应共存；色噪声Keldysh模型中有限关联时间填充赝能隙、合并谱峰并窄化线宽。

themes.title: 受限与界面诱导的新奇有序及实验证据
themes.summary: 单层1T′-MoTe₂的条纹CDW把低能态重组为准一维通道，静电掺杂削弱横向绝缘响应并驱动二维超导；HTG在约1.7°下形成超莫尔畴，畴内平带与远程带间约40 meV能隙，畴壁边缘态谱学均匀并与谷保护拓扑边缘模式计算一致；界面极性决定LaCoO3-SrIrO3中AHE能否出现，电子掺杂SrIrO3出现AHE而空穴掺杂被抑制；扭曲铜氧化物约瑟夫森结的Shapiro台阶呈nhf/3e序列，指向3e隧穿过程。

2026-11-06.caveat: 需核对：SteelBench的样品条件、数据规模与适用范围；热流敏感性图的温度、尺寸外推与力常数误差，以及约100 K以下残留分量的归属；FNO与PolyGPT等代理/生成模型仅报告模拟或生成评估，缺少实验制备或合成验证；拓扑量子存储的N≥40为保守充分界，阈值论文未给数值；3e隧穿、超莫尔畴与AHE结果需核对样品参数、温度与统计代表性；色噪声Keldysh模型未给γ的定量边界。以上均不应外推为领域趋势。

2026-11-05.headline: 从对称性与噪声到可观测输运：多体系中的约束、鲁棒性与边界
2026-11-05.overview: 本期论文横跨格点场论、量子输运、磁性材料、软物质与数值方法，共同关注“对称性/拓扑/噪声如何约束可观测响应”。一条路线从精确对称性出发，讨论手征对称、宇称选择定则、陈数与边缘模式如何决定谱与输运；另一条路线关注无序、耗散与驱动，考察噪声诱导拓扑、弱局域化、渗流开启与热化。材料侧则围绕镍酸盐、交错磁体、氢化物与超导结给出结构—配对—输运的联系。方法上出现张量网络、变分蒙特卡洛、机器学习势与第一性原理流程化等工具。各文证据强度差异明显，部分仅为片段摘要。

themes.title: 精确对称性与拓扑约束下的谱和输运
themes.summary: 多篇工作把对称性作为可检验判据：格点手征算符的无序平均严格反对易但轴矢指标为零，说明精确手征对称与非厄米性可并存却不重现反常；二维晶体电子-声子耦合存在镜宇称选择定则，Sc2BCH4中禁戒矩阵元数值为零，块体MgB2仅在镜不变面严格；格点Chern-Simons在圆柱上给出精确局域于两边界的手征边缘模式；量子霍尔条的平台边缘随电流方向移动，由面内C2协变性支配。这些结果共同显示对称性既限制允许通道，也决定边界响应。

themes.title: 无序、耗散与噪声：破坏还是赋予鲁棒性
themes.summary: 另一组证据表明噪声与无序的作用依赖具体通道：退相位噪声不破坏手性量子行走的输运不对称，反而使其获得拓扑鲁棒性并可驱动相变；单层MoS2晶体管的表观金属-绝缘体转变可由霍尔密度塌缩与激活能消失解释为渗流开启；FQH-超导结中耗散子能隙模式可解释非量子化边缘电导的两类温度行为；零噪声外推在噪声破坏守恒律时对噪声强度呈非解析依赖。这些工作把“噪声是否抹去信号”转化为可区分的机制问题。

themes.title: 关联与配对：从模型到候选材料
themes.summary: 强关联体系中的配对竞争与磁性基态是本期另一条线：双层Hubbard模型中空穴掺杂诱导自旋条纹，主导配对由d波交叉为s±波；蜂窝网络变分蒙特卡洛显示反对称自旋轨道耦合可使最低变分能量由f波转为手性p波；三谷2e/3任意子气在双体束缚共振附近给出电子坐标下Cooper对非对角长程序；双层镍酸盐中破坏层间镜面对称可导致配对密度波并牵涉安德森定理适用性。另有ZnCoP2O7被报告为阻挫诱导自旋液体基态，但摘要证据有限。

themes.title: 结构、应变与热输运的定量刻画
themes.summary: 材料结构与输运的定量联系在多篇中出现：κ-Ga2O3薄膜面外热导率仅1.83–2.26 W/m·K，随厚度弱增、随温度下降；β-Ga2O3/SiC异质界面引入纳米晶Si中间层后界面热导达165 MW m^-2 K^-1；同位素纯立方GeC计算给出室温热导率1018 W/m·K，并归因于强同位素增强与较弱四声子散射；Ni_xNbS2中插层Ni由无序经2×2与√3×√3有序到条纹有序，层间距在x=1/4出现极小。这些结果把微观结构参数与宏观热/结构响应对应起来。

themes.title: 计算方法与可编程平台：从算法保证到量子模拟架构
themes.summary: 方法侧出现若干可复用工具：SK模型给出N与1/ε均为多项式的(1-ε)近似算法及有限维定量保证；旋转—采样—反旋转行列式发现在N2拉伸构型下5000次采样达化学精度，而常规QSCI需20000次；DefectSkills把点缺陷第一性原理流程编码为AI代理技能；激子-极化激元波导网络被提出用于可编程层间耦合与XY自旋模拟，并报告宏观网络中能量降低逾50倍、标准差缩小6倍。这些工作分别提供算法保证、流程规范与物理平台方案，但多数尚缺实验验证。

2026-11-05.caveat: 阅读时需逐篇核对：多篇PRB条目仅有截断的RSS摘要，结论与定量证据无法从摘要核实；部分arXiv摘要明确为理论、模拟或理想化条件（如自旋投影守恒、无噪声模拟、非反应MD、热力学极限），不能外推为实验结论；涉及“最高值”“首次”“普适”等表述应回到全文核对比较基准与误差；摘要未给出的样品条件、参数范围、有限尺寸效应与统计不确定度不应补推。

2026-11-04.headline: 从几何与对称性出发：跨体系的约束、相变与输运
2026-11-04.overview: 本期论文围绕一个共同问题展开：体系的宏观响应能否由几何、对称性或少数低维结构量约束。路线大致分三类：一是用热力学几何、共形代数、尺度函数等抽象结构给出普适约束或反常权衡；二是用对称性论证与精确可解点判定相变、拓扑相与边缘态是否稳定；三是用数值与机器学习方法在具体材料或模型中检验这些约束，并给出可测量的判据。不同路线对“普适”的界定并不一致，有的依赖慢驱动、大N或平均场近似，有的依赖特定晶格与参数窗口，阅读时需区分严格结论与数值证据。

themes.title: 几何与代数结构对动力学和响应的约束
themes.summary: 多篇工作把响应归因于几何或代数结构而非具体微观细节：慢驱动区存在冷却更多却耗散更少的反常权衡，其出现有几何必要条件；临界基态可重构完整全局共形代数；一维扩散的重整化普适类由尺度函数决定；纠缠熵的普适项在指定边界条件下不受选择影响，但对应非酉映射的边界条件可改变这些项。这些结论各自限定在慢驱动、正则化或一维过阻尼等条件下。

themes.title: 对称性判定相变、拓扑与边缘态
themes.summary: 对称性论证被用于判断相是否稳定及边缘态是否存在：时间反演与宇称共同作用可在Liouvillian中强制Kramers简并；自旋轨道锁定使三角Dirac自旋液体对XXZ各向异性与键依赖耦合保持稳定；交错磁序可打开螺旋边缘态能隙而保留体狄拉克点，形成高阶拓扑相；精确Rokhsar-Kivelson点给出简并基态与一级相变；手性冰与主导手性顶点区域均呈临界，长程行为对应自由无质量场。这些多为对称性证明或精确构造，适用范围依赖绝热连续性、晶格几何等前提。

themes.title: 数值与机器学习方法检验模型预言
themes.summary: 若干工作用数值或机器学习方法在具体体系中检验理论预言：无限柱面DMRG显示扭转MoTe₂窄Chern带中排斥相互作用可产生手性f波拓扑超导；实时多轨道杂质求解器C³L与QMC高度一致而成本低四到五个数量级；TT-SCHA无需随机采样即可给出合金自由能，与65,536原子分子动力学相差0.13 meV/atom；VP-DDBM在留出热梯度下长时预测误差低于确定性基线并保留细枝晶结构。这些证据受模型维度、势函数与训练数据范围限制。

themes.title: 输运与响应的非互易及非常规通道
themes.summary: 输运研究给出多种非互易或非常规响应：Kekulé石墨烯超晶格隧道结可承载有限谷超电流并实现无耗散谷二极管效应；交错磁与拓扑绝缘体异质结在无外磁场时出现横向微分电导，其大小与符号由奈尔矢量取向和化学势对称性决定；菱形堆叠石墨烯的反常霍尔响应被归因于谷极化下Wilson环路径干涉而非Haldane型平衡环电流；手性极限下对称性可抑制贝里曲率通道，使量子度规成为光学与非线性霍尔响应的唯一来源。这些多为理论预言，实验验证程度不一。

themes.title: 材料表征中的边界与定量约束
themes.summary: 实验与表征类工作给出带明确边界的定量约束：单层FeSe/SrTiO₃的隧穿谱经统计分析与针尖高度依赖回归，将超导能隙约束在6–13 meV；晶胞内约瑟夫森扫描隧道谱显示氧位点响应增强、铜位点与对角方向受抑，可由符号相反的配对贡献干涉解释；限流电化学可将埋藏Ge/Si界面转为横向连续纳米级自由表面，Raman显示残余张应变约从0.10%降至0.05%；Ta基S-I-S结在150 mm晶圆工艺下0.4 μm²结的结分散低至2.0%。这些数值均限于所测样品、温度与工艺窗口。

2026-11-04.caveat: 阅读时需核对：各理论结论的适用条件（慢驱动区、大N极限、平均场近似、绝热连续性、一维过阻尼等）是否与所讨论体系匹配；数值证据的有限尺寸外推、误差范围与参数窗口是否给出；实验类数值是否限于特定样品、温度、磁场或工艺条件，摘要未给出的置信区间与统计量不应自行补全；部分条目为RSS片段或综述，结论可能被截断，需回原文核实。

papers.title: Flat-band systems: A platform to realize the moments of Quantum Metric
papers.abstract: The quantum metric is a fundamental geometric property of Bloch bands that governs a wide range of physical phenomena, yet experimentally accessing it remains challenging. We show that the momentum-space variation of the quantum metric can be probed through the real-space dynamics of a Gaussian wave packet prepared in an isolated flat band. Following the application of a weak constant force, we demonstrate analytically that the leading order change in the wave-packet variance is linear in time and contains a contribution proportional to the wave-packet averaged gradient of the quantum-metric trace. This geometric contribution remains finite despite the absence of band dispersion. We illustrate the effect using a gapped Lieb lattice with an exactly flat middle band and vanishing Berry curvature, allowing the quantum-metric contribution to the spreading to be isolated. The numerical results agree with the analytical prediction and confirm the quantum-metric contribution to the wave-packet spreading. The required lattice preparation, tunable hopping amplitudes, applied force, and density measurements are compatible with established ultracold-atom techniques, providing a possible platform for observing the predicted response. Our results establish wave-packet spreading as a dynamical probe of quantum geometry in flat-band systems.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论分析结合数值计算；摘要含解析推导与数值验证；研究对象：具有精确平带的gapped Lieb lattice（有能隙Lieb晶格），中间带平坦且Berry曲率为零
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 在孤立平带中制备的高斯波包，在弱恒定力下其方差随时间的线性变化包含正比于量子度规迹梯度的波包平均贡献，该几何贡献在无带色散时仍有限。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：如何在实验上探测Bloch带的量子度规（quantum metric），特别是其动量空间变化，并区分其与带色散、Berry曲率等贡献。
证据与比较：解析表明波包方差领头阶随时间线性变化，并含量子度规迹梯度的波包平均项；在中间带精确平坦且Berry曲率为零的gapped Lieb lattice上数值结果与解析预测一致，确认量子度规对波包展宽的贡献。
papers.method_zh: 对孤立平带中的高斯波包施加弱恒定力，解析推导方差随时间的演化；用gapped Lieb lattice进行数值计算验证。

english_guide.finding: The leading-order change in the variance of a Gaussian wave packet in an isolated flat band under a weak constant force is linear in time and contains a contribution proportional to the wave-packet averaged gradient of the quantum-metric trace, which remains finite without band dispersion.
english_guide.question: How can the momentum-space variation of the quantum metric be probed experimentally and isolated from band dispersion and Berry curvature contributions?
english_guide.evidence: Analytics show a linear-in-time variance change with a quantum-metric term; numerics on a gapped Lieb lattice with an exactly flat middle band and vanishing Berry curvature agree with the analytical prediction and confirm the quantum-metric contribution to wave-packet spreading.
english_guide.method: Analytical derivation of Gaussian wave-packet variance dynamics in an isolated flat band under a weak constant force, with numerical verification on a gapped Lieb lattice.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state that wave-packet spreading is established as a dynamical probe of quantum geometry in flat-band systems and that the required lattice preparation, tunable hopping amplitudes, applied force, and density measurements are compatible with established ultracold-atom techniques.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify finite-temperature, disorder, interaction, or weak-force validity conditions; experimental feasibility is stated as compatibility with ultracold-atom techniques, without measured data.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称将波包展宽确立为平带系统中量子几何的动力学探针，并指出所需条件与现有超冷原子技术兼容。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明有限温度、无序、相互作用及弱力近似适用范围；实验可行性仅为作者所述与超冷原子技术兼容，未提供实测数据。

papers.title: Direct transition from a fractional Chern insulator to a topological superconductor
papers.abstract: We find numerical evidence for a direct continuous transition from a Laughlin fractional Chern insulator (FCI) to a $c_-=3/2$ topological superconductor (TSC), driven by increasing bandwidth at filling $ν=1/3$ in a repulsively interacting Chern band. At the critical point, the electron correlation length diverges at momentum away from the reference Fermi surface. We develop a generalized theory of superconducting-vortex proliferation for this transition. Magnetic translation organizes the vortices into six valleys, so translation-preserving proliferation requires additional gauge fields. The resulting theory reproduces the momentum structure of the critical spectrum and captures the divergent electron correlation. Upon doping away from commensurate filling, the theory gives rise to a superconducting dome. These results are consistent with an anyonic origin of the topological superconductivity in the absence of a weak-coupling Fermi-surface instability.

papers.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
papers.abstract: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field. We further propose an experimental realization of an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field in a spinor condensate. Our results can be generalized to other non-compact groups and higher dimensions, providing a geometric framework for entanglement control, selective amplification, and engineering energy transfer.

papers.title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate the collision and fracture processes of ball milling based on a minimal model of a three-sphere geometry using discrete element method (DEM) simulations combined with Christensen-type and Weibull-type normalized fracture criteria. The outcome of the brittle target particle (ejected versus trapped, fractured versus intact) depends on the impact geometry and velocity. We develop a reduced three-sphere collision description in which trapping is governed by impact geometry and friction, while fracture inside the trapping regime is evaluated from DEM output using stress-based and contact-force-based normalized criteria. The trapping regime follows a closed-form geometric condition, while the critical conditions for fracture vary with impact angle, obliquity angle, impact velocity, and particle size ratio. Head-on collisions with larger size ratios require lower critical impact velocities for fracture.

papers.title: Synaptic Multi-Weight Wafer-Scale Domain Wall Magnetic Tunnel Junctions Driven by Spin Orbit Torque
papers.abstract: Spintronic synaptic devices based on magnetic random access memory (MRAM) are a rapidly evolving class within the analog neuromorphic architecture. However, obtaining the multi-weight or analog behavior desired for improved neural network inference accuracy in scaled MRAM remains a challenge. In this study, we demonstrate and tune up to eight distinct resistance levels in 300 mm wafer-scale magnetic tunnel junction artificial synapses driven by spin orbit torque. By varying the applied in-plane field, multi-weight resistance states emerge through domain wall nucleation and pinning. These multi-weight states appear stochastically and can be addressed with an iterative programming algorithm to program a specific resistance. Electromagnetic simulations indicate the multiple states are due to domain wall nucleation mediated by in-plane field and applied voltage. Implementation of the measured multi-weight devices in a neural network yields a 96.1% inference accuracy using the MNIST dataset if all devices provide the same number of multi-weight states. When experimental device-to-device variation is included, the accuracy is 48.6%. Overall, this work demonstrates a route towards multi-weight artificial synapse MRAM, establishing a path towards scalable neuromorphic systems based on spintronics.

papers.title: Anisotropy lifts topological protection of transport in pumped spin chains
papers.abstract: We investigate the prospect of topological spin pumping and transport in a dimerized spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ anisotropic XY chain with tunable in-plane anisotropy. Through a Jordan-Wigner transformation, the system maps onto an extended Rice-Mele-type fermionic model whose momentum-space band structure exhibits gapped regions characterized by nonzero Chern numbers ($\pm 1$) as well as trivial and gapless regimes. Conventional momentum-space analysis therefore predicts quantized Thouless-type spin pumping in parts of the Chern number diagram. However, real-space time evolution under open boundary conditions reveals that the spin transport is generally not quantized away from the isotropic limit. In the anisotropic regime, eigen-energy states within the transporting subspace hybridize during the driving cycle, leading to a transport that depends on details of the driving protocol. Quantized pumping and transport survive only in the isotropic limit, where the Hamiltonian reduces to decoupled Rice-Mele sectors and the transported spin component is conserved. Our results demonstrate that momentum-space topological invariants alone do not guarantee quantized spin transport in anisotropic spin chains. More broadly, they show that the conventional Thouless-pumping framework does not straightforwardly extend to situations where the transported quantity is not conserved, highlighting the importance of real-space diagnostics in topological transport phenomena.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
papers.abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.

papers.title: Multimagnon bound states in the polarized phase of anisotropic antiferromagnets
papers.abstract: We investigate single-ion bound magnon states in the high-field polarized phase of uniaxial antiferromagnets. By solving the two-particle problem exactly, we determine the dispersion of bound magnon pairs both below and above the continuum. We also obtain rigorous bounds on their binding energies by using the Gershgorin circle theorem. For spin-1 easy-axis systems, two-magnon bound states with zero total momentum emerge as low-energy excitations once the ratio of single-ion anisotropy to exchange exceeds a threshold value. As the field decreases, magnon pairs condense, driving a transition into a spin-nematic phase. Beyond the two-magnon problem, we develop a general strong-coupling approach that describes $n$-magnon single-ion bound states ($n\leq 2S$) in large-$S$ easy-axis antiferromagnets. The Bose-Einstein condensation of these multi-magnon excitations yields a rich hierarchy of field-induced multipolar phases stabilized by single-ion anisotropy. Comparisons with recent experiments on Na$_2$BaNi(PO$_4$)$_2$ and Sr$_2$CoGe$_2$O$_7$ illustrate the quantitative power of our theory.

papers.title: Typical number and stability of equilibria in large non-reciprocal complex systems
papers.abstract: We consider a prototypical class of dynamics of $N\gg 1$ degrees of freedom subject to two competing terms, one favoring relaxation to a trivial equilibrium and one taking the form of a Gaussian force field promoting the emergence of many local equilibria. The latter is a non-gradient field, i.e. it includes a non-reciprocal component with a tunable strength. For this model, we compute the quenched complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the typical number of equilibria, resolved by stability index. We compare it with the annealed complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the average number of equilibria. We show that the two coincide only in the fully non-reciprocal limit: for any finite degree of reciprocity, typical realizations contain exponentially fewer equilibria than predicted by the average count. Increasing reciprocity enhances the discrepancy between the two. The quenched complexity depends explicitly on the covariance of the random force field and on the degree of non-reciprocity: the universality observed at the annealed level breaks down. The average counting of equilibria correctly identifies the location of the topology trivialization transition, but it does not capture the typical organization of equilibria near this transition, nor the stability index of the dominant equilibria.

papers.title: Active model B+ from run-and-tumble particles on a triangular lattice
papers.abstract: Active model B+ (AMB+) explains how motility-induced phase separation can be arrested by reverse Ostwald ripening, but its coefficients have not been derived from a microscopic lattice model that shows it. We provide an exact hydrodynamic description of a six-polarity lattice gas on a hexagonal geometry and employ a full gradient expansion with angular-harmonic elimination to rigorously derive AMB+ with every coefficient fixed by the Péclet number Pe. Near the critical point (3/4, 4), coarsening is ordinary; further away, field theory predicts reverse Ostwald ripening of vapor bubbles above Pe $> 4 \sqrt{3}$, and simulations show long-lived bubbly states.

papers.title: Spin supersolid in triangular lattice easy-axis spin-1/2 antiferromagnet: a fermionic parton perspective
papers.abstract: We study the supersolid order of the spin-1/2 easy-axis XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice using a fermionic parton mean-field theory built on the $π$-flux Dirac spin liquid, with the mean-field order generated by an on-site spinon interaction term and nearest-neighbor (anisotropic) spin couplings. The collective modes are obtained using the random-phase approximation (RPA). In a finite parameter region, we find the Y state as a self-consistent solution, together with the competing Y' state, which is a $90^\circ$-rotated Y state inside the order plane. The mean-field energy favors Y', even though the two states are exactly degenerate in the classical limit. However, the Y state can become lower in energy when higher-order corrections due to the fluctuations of the collective modes are considered. The Y state can also be stabilized on the mean-field level by applying small external fields, which we do in two different ways: moment-aligned local field and uniform field along the easy axis. In both cases, the RPA calculation for the stabilized Y state gives a roton minimum at the $M$ point in the excitation spectrum. A gapped pseudo-Goldstone mode above the gapless Goldstone mode is obtained as well, which has also been observed experimentally. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of tuning the spinon interaction strength and the anisotropy in spin couplings in our phenomenological model. Comparison with the recent numerical and experimental results is also discussed.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Forgetting in a Bounded Hopfield Network
papers.abstract: A memory that keeps learning must also forget. The Hopfield network does not: beyond a critical number of stored patterns it falls into a state of total confusion and retrieves none of them. Parisi showed in 1986 that bounding the synaptic strength cures this pathology, since the clipping of the couplings gradually erases the oldest memories and leaves room for the new ones. In this paper we provide a thermodynamic description of the resulting network, known as the Hopfield-Parisi model. Starting from the learning rule, we show that the network is equivalent to a Hopfield model whose patterns are weighted according to their age, superimposed on a Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, both governed by the synaptic bound: a larger bound makes the memory longer, but also noisier. The theory of nonlinear networks developed in the eighties already provides, through the heuristic replica method, the equations that govern this model at any temperature, but to the best of our knowledge they have been solved only at zero temperature. We rederive them at the replica symmetric level through Guerra's interpolation and solve them at finite temperature, obtaining the phase diagram of the model together with its memory horizon, namely the largest age at which a pattern can still be retrieved. The solution shows that forgetting acts on the signal alone, the noise being the same for patterns of every age, and that the horizon is maximal at an intermediate bound which is essentially insensitive to temperature. Monte Carlo simulations of networks trained with the original learning rule support these predictions.

papers.title: Finite-element reconstruction of molten-zone dynamics and chemical segregation in optical floating-zone grown Ni--Mn--Ga
papers.abstract: Homogeneous single-crystal growth of Ni--Mn--Ga magnetic shape-memory alloys is limited by incongruent melting, Mn reactivity, and longitudinal composition segregation. We report a modified optical floating-zone method in which growth is performed inside a transparent sapphire crucible, stabilising the molten zone while preserving optical heating and visual monitoring. The resulting crystals show improved growth reproducibility and controlled macroscopic geometry. To interpret the measured segregation profiles, a transient finite-element heat-transfer model in COMSOL Multiphysics was coupled to an effective molten-zone mass-balance calculation. The model reveals that the local solidification velocity is not fixed by the imposed translation speed but varies strongly as the molten-zone geometry evolves. The calculated solidification-front geometry is independently supported by EBSD analysis of a quenched growth interface, while the coupled mass-balance calculation reproduces the dominant features of the measured composition profiles. These results show that deviations from ideal Scheil--Pfann behaviour arise from the evolving molten-zone geometry and solidification conditions. The experimentally constrained model therefore provides a practical means of reconstructing otherwise inaccessible growth conditions and a basis for optimisation of sapphire-confined floating-zone growth of incongruently melting alloys.

papers.title: Experimental Evidence for Type-I Superconductivity in $\mathrm{OsB_2}$
papers.abstract: Since the discovery of superconductivity in $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, metal diborides have attracted significant attention. Among these, osmium diboride ($\mathrm{OsB_2}$), crystallizing in an orthorhombic structure (space group $Pmmn$) with puckered boron layers, has been classified as a low-$κ$ Type-II superconductor ($T_c \approx 2.1~\mathrm{K}$). Here, we report experimental evidence establishing that $\mathrm{OsB_2}$ is in fact a rare nonelemental Type-I superconductor. Our identification is supported by three primary experimental hallmarks: (i) a pronounced Differential Paramagnetic Effect (DPE) peak in AC susceptibility ($χ_{ac}$) measurements under static DC magnetic fields, signaling the intermediate state; (ii) a field-induced crossover to a divergent first-order phase transition in specific heat ($C/T$); and (iii) pronounced magnetic hysteresis in field-ramped transitions indicative of supercooling.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic interaction in Lattice Fokker Planck for dilute polymer dynamics
papers.abstract: We extend the BGK-type kinetic model for polymer dumbbells and its lattice Boltzmann implementation by incorporating hydrodynamic interaction (HI) effects to accurately recover the slow-variable dynamics governed by the Smoluchowski equation. Unlike Brownian dynamics approaches, which demand the computationally expensive evaluation of the square root of the configuration-dependent diffusion tensor at every time step, this kinetic method is straightforward to implement and avoids such overhead entirely. Consequently, it achieves a significant reduction in computational cost. We validate the model in steady and transient shear flows, demonstrating its ability to capture the distinct signatures of hydrodynamic interactions on bulk rheological properties.

papers.title: Coherent phase slips in coupled rings: from weak to strong interactions
papers.abstract: We study the coherent transfer of circulation between two weakly coupled lattice rings of ultracold bosons, in which a persistent current initially prepared in one ring oscillates back and forth between the rings without net transfer of particles. Combining Bose--Hubbard simulations with their Gross--Pitaevskii and quantum phase model limits, we show that similar current oscillations arise from two distinct microscopic mechanisms. At weak interactions, particles in each occupied momentum mode tunnel independently between the rings, leading to a transfer time inversely proportional to the inter-ring tunnelling, extensive particle-number fluctuations and entanglement distributed over many Schmidt components; this mode-exchange dynamics is suppressed by self-trapping as the interactions increase. At stronger interactions and large filling, in the phase-dominated regime, circulation is instead transferred through a second-order collective process between many-body persistent-current states, with a transfer time scaling as the inverse square of the inter-ring tunnelling in the weak-link limit. Number fluctuations then remain of order one instead of growing with the particle number, and within each number sector the system evolves into coherent superpositions of two many-body configurations, distinguished by which ring carries the circulation. The entanglement accessible under number-conserving operations therefore reaches up to approximately one bit. We propose a quench protocol to prepare the initial state and estimate transfer times within reach of current ring-lattice experiments, identifying coupled rings as a platform to study coherent quantum phase slips and to manipulate persistent-current states.

papers.title: Thermodynamic geometry of three coupled Ising spins: exact curvature, frustration and bond anisotropy
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic curvature is widely used as a diagnostic of interactions and phase transitions, yet its interpretation is usually tested only in the thermodynamic limit. Small spin clusters are physically relevant in their own right, since a macroscopic sample of independent molecular trimers or a few-qubit quantum simulator is governed exactly by the few-spin partition function. They also provide the only setting in which the geometry can be obtained in closed form together with its full dependence on the interaction topology. We study the Fisher-Rao (Ruppeiner) geometry of three Ising spins with arbitrary pairwise couplings in a longitudinal field. This cluster interpolates continuously between an open chain and a geometrically frustrated triangle. For the symmetric triangle we obtain the scalar curvature in closed form. It vanishes on the noninteracting line and on a line of fixed field-to-temperature ratio that does not depend on the coupling, which coincides with the inflection point of the single-spin susceptibility. The near-zero behaviour is therefore exactly linear and reflects analyticity rather than critical scaling. In the frustrated antiferromagnetic regime the curvature remains finite and negative down to zero temperature. A general low-temperature formula relates this plateau to the change in magnetization content between the degenerate ground manifold and its first excitation. Any bond anisotropy destroys the plateau below a crossover temperature that depends only logarithmically on the anisotropy, so the curvature is an extremely sensitive detector of exact ground-state degeneracy. On the ferromagnetic side the zero-temperature curvature is universal for all couplings, whereas additional zero lines in anisotropic clusters track field-induced crossings of excited levels.

papers.title: The polar discontinuity picture in nickelate superlattices: comparison of the insulating and metallic phases
papers.abstract: We present a first-principles study of the formal-charge polar discontinuity in superlattices of BaTiO$_3$ interfaced with SmNiO$_3$ or BiNiO$_3$, comparing the results for the insulating and metallic nickelate phases. Polar discontinuities arising from differently charged layers in perovskites are well-studied in heterostructures such as LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$, and recently, signatures consistent with such a polar discontinuity have been observed in systems where the formally charged layers would reside in a metal. We first identify signatures of the polar discontinuity in the structure and the density of states of superlattices with BaTiO$_3$ and insulating BiNiO$_3$, and find partial screening by modification of the BiNiO$_3$ charge disproportionation pattern analogous to our previous study on BaTiO$_3$/SmNiO$_3$. We then examine superlattices constructed from the corresponding metallic nickelate phases and find that, despite the presence of screening charges, the qualitative interfacial response is remarkably similar to that of the insulating counterparts. We show that the metallic screening charges have little influence on the apparent formal-charge polar discontinuity and discuss practical limitations of the polar-discontinuity picture when interpreting and quantifying screening at metallic nickelate/ferroelectric interfaces.

papers.title: Key role of orbital exchange in CoO magnetism
papers.abstract: Co ions in the antiferromagnetic phase of CoO are known to possess a substantial orbital moment, making this material promising for orbitronic applications. However, intersite exchange interactions involving these orbital degrees of freedom remain poorly quantified, and their role in CoO magnetism is unclear. Here, we derive a full low-energy effective Hamiltonian for CoO, including orbital exchange terms, using an ab initio force-theorem approach based on DFT+dynamical mean-field theory. We find sizable orbital interactions, with quadrupolar orbital exchange emerging as the dominant nearest-neighbor term. The collinear antiferromagnetic order obtained from the effective Hamiltonian features magnetic moments tilted away from the pseudocubic <001> direction and an orbital contribution amounting to about one-third of the total moment, in agreement with experimental estimates. We show that the moment tilting originates from the combined effect of orbital and spin-orbital exchange interactions. The same interactions also produce a prominent splitting of the lowest excitation band. By directly modeling the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) intensity, we further show that the characteristic column-like structures previously observed in CoO INS provide a clear fingerprint of orbital exchange. We also discuss possible impact of our findings for further advances in the field of complex collective excitations, their transport properties and applications in the realm of orbitronics.

papers.title: Ferroelectric control of magnetic coupling in a Cr dimer adsorbed on $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric substrates offer a route to controlling magnetic interactions in low-dimensional systems through polarization-dependent changes in local bonding and electronic structure. Here, using first-principles calculations, we investigate the adsorption of 3$d$ transition-metal atoms and dimers on monolayer $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ and identify Cr as a stable dimer configuration on both polar surfaces. Reversing the ferroelectric polarization drives a pronounced change in its magnetic coupling: the AFM state is favored for one polarization, whereas the FM and AFM configurations become nearly degenerate for the opposite one. Analysis of the spin density, projected electronic states, and Wannier Hamiltonians reveals concomitant changes in the direct Cr-Cr hopping and in the interaction with the bridging Se atom. In particular, enhanced Cr-Se hybridization and Se spin polarization, together with a strong reduction of the direct two-center Cr-Cr hopping, point to a polarization-dependent balance between direct and substrate-mediated exchange contributions. These results show how ferroelectric polarization can tune magnetic interactions in an atomically defined 2D hybrid system.

papers.title: First-order condensation and meniscus pinning in finite open wedges
papers.abstract: We study first-order condensation in finite open wedges using classical density functional theory (DFT) and compare the resulting microscopic phase behaviour with recent macroscopic predictions. Two geometries are considered: a symmetric wedge formed by two identical inclined walls and an asymmetric wedge formed by a vertical and an inclined wall. The DFT calculations confirm the two condensed morphologies predicted for the symmetric wedge and the three morphologies predicted for the asymmetric wedge and their emergence depending on the wedge size, opening angle, and wall contact angle. Under partial-wetting conditions, the microscopic phase boundaries are in nearly perfect quantitative agreement with the macroscopic predictions, including reentrant changes between pinned and depinned meniscus configurations and the appearance of the semi-double-pinned state in the asymmetric wedge. Under complete-wetting conditions, the DFT phase diagrams retain the topology predicted by the macroscopic theory, but the single-pinned region is systematically enlarged. This shift is attributed to adsorbed liquid films, which reduce the effective width available to the gas and thereby increase the effective aspect ratio of the confinement.

papers.title: Closed-form solution for semi-symmetric folding of waterbomb tessellations
papers.abstract: Rigid-origami folding has versatile applications in the fields of architecture, engineering, medicine and aerospace. Given the design parameters of a single waterbomb cell, the global geometry of the origami tessellated shell at an intermediate state of folding is directly determined. Even though existing numerical methods of rigid-origami can be used to describe geometric forms, algebraic solutions of the waterbomb folding kinematics and tessellations reduce the algorithmic complexity and determine the range of admissible configurations exactly. The existing analytical solution for a symmetrically folded waterbomb cell and tessellation is extended to the case of a cell folded semi-symmetrically, i.e. a cell with a 180° rotation symmetry. The algebraic derivation provides the solution for the entire folding process. The resulting functional relationship between the design parameters and the 3D cell geometry of the folded waterbomb cell enables efficient studies of achievable shell geometries. This development facilitates a deeper understanding of the correspondence between the geometric parameters of a single waterbomb cell and the statically relevant geometric properties, i.e. the shell curvature and the effective cross-sectional height. The systematic description of this correspondence provides the basis for innovative design concepts using modern cementitious composites, e.g. textile-reinforced concrete, to produce thin-walled, high-performance, lightweight shells.

papers.title: When Molecular Dimerization Induces Magnetic Bi-Stability at the Metal-Organic Interface
papers.abstract: We present a method to create metal-organic dimer complexes by on-surface assembly on a metal substrate using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS). We demonstrate that a dimer of Mn-Phthalocyanine (MnPc)2 on a Ag(111) surface can be switched between two stable configurations upon a small conformational change controlled by STM manipulation. By means of density-functional theory calculations, it is found that the two conformations correspond to an antiferromagnetic (AFM) and a ferromagnetic (FM) state respectively. Directly coordinated Mn atoms of the dimer lead to an AFM-coupling whereas indirectly coordinated (shifted) Mn atoms lead to a FM-coupling. Rarely seen in a molecular- dimers with transition-metal atoms, the FM-AFM-FM transition is thus readily on-surface accessible. Furthermore, the two configurations of the switch are easily identified by their Kondo states, opening interesting routes in terms of both, writing (FM versus AFM states) and reading. These results pave the experimental route toward dimer-based materials with complex magnetic structures of potential interest for application in spintronics, logics and computing.

papers.title: Microscopic Origin and Josephson Signatures of $d$-Wave Superconductivity in Monolayer FeSe
papers.abstract: Monolayer FeSe on SrTiO$_3$ exhibits high-temperature superconductivity with an electron-only Fermi surface, raising fundamental questions about its unconventional pairing mechanism. Motivated by recent Josephson scanning tunneling microscopy evidence for nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity, we investigate the microscopic role of the Fe $d_{xy}$ orbital using an experimentally constrained multiorbital theory. A tight-binding model fitted to quasiparticle interference and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals substantial $d_{xy}$ character near the Fermi level and dominant nearest-neighbor hopping, in contrast to the conventional kinetic-frustration picture of iron-based superconductors. Both itinerant spin-fluctuation calculations and strong-coupling exchange approaches favor a robust $d$-wave pairing state, whose interband pairing components allow a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum. We further establish a symmetry-based selection rule for spatial Josephson tunneling, revealing characteristic bond-centered maxima and mirror-enforced interference zeros that distinguish $d$-wave pairing from competing $s$-wave states. These symmetry-enforced nodal lines survive near Fe-site impurities, while a pronounced contrast between the $d$- and $s$-wave Josephson patterns persists around vortices despite the loss of mirror protection. Our results connect the unconventional $d_{xy}$ electronic structure to nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity and demonstrate the power of spatial Josephson interference for resolving pairing symmetry in multiorbital superconductors.

papers.title: Galois conjugation, droplet growth, and the differential transcendence of the Ising model in nonzero field
papers.abstract: The square-lattice Ising model is exactly solvable in zero magnetic field, but the scope of exact solutions at nonzero field remains unresolved. We show that, at every fixed dimensionless field $H=h/(k_BT)\ne 0$, its free energy and magnetization obey no algebraic differential equation in the coupling $K=J/(k_BT)$. This excludes Onsager-type formulas and broad classes of special-function expressions. Previous work left open a countable set of fields with algebraic-integer fugacities. We eliminate these exceptions using Galois conjugation and the large-order growth of droplets of reversed spins. At conjugate fugacities outside the unit circle, nearly square droplets produce coefficient growth incompatible with an algebraic differential equation. We prove that cancellations cannot remove this growth in the full pressure series. The free-energy result also holds for the Lieb lattice and square lattices with equal-length chain decorations and uniform coupling and field. In every dimension $d\ge2$, we additionally resolve fields for which $e^{-2|H|}$ has a real algebraic conjugate greater than one.

papers.title: Splay ostracism on ferroelectric nematic shells
papers.abstract: Ostracism was the practice in use in Athens and other ancient Greek cities to send into exile citizens whose influence was deemed to be dangerous. Quite similarly, splay ostracism is here the approximation that bans splay distortion from thin films of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals on a curved shell in space. This reduces to a mere geometric problem the quest for equilibria of director vortexes and the walls isolating them, as splay ostracism requires the director field lines to be everywhere orthogonal to systems of geodesics on the shell. Consequences of this theorem are explored for shells with Gaussian curvature of either sign. The resulting quasi static dynamics reveals both cases where walls escape from the shell and cases where they are trapped on it, with possibly different reflections on the vortex dynamics.

papers.title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
papers.abstract: We find that MOF-5 supports both long-lived phonons and linker vibrations whose split spectra signal a breakdown of the phonon quasiparticle approximation. Combining mode-projected molecular dynamics spectra with spectral Wigner heat transport, we resolve two contrasting transport channels: low-frequency particle-like phonon propagation decreases strongly from 200 to 500 K, whereas wave-like phonon coherence remains nearly constant and supplies about half the intrinsic conductivity at 500 K. A phenomenological extrinsic scattering model provides a plausible explanation for the discrepancy between calculated and measured conductivities in terms of both its magnitude and temperature dependence. We also identify signatures of phonon quasiparticle breakdown in the linker vibrations of ZIF-8 and HKUST-1, indicating that this feature extends to other metal-organic frameworks.

papers.title: Zero-Point Renormalization Reshapes the Shift Current: The Role of Electron-Phonon Coupling
papers.abstract: Shift current (SC) drives the bulk photovoltaic effect, holding promise for near-instantaneous, low-dissipation photodetection and energy conversion. The current understanding of SC relies primarily on a single-particle picture, in which the SC is determined purely by band dispersion. While many-body effects from directly excited quasiparticles, such as excitons, magnons and phonons, have been explored, the renormalization of electronic states by quantum virtual-phonon coupling --- inherent in essentially all solids and particularly decisive for transport --- remains unaddressed. Here, using first-principles calculations, we identify this missing channel --- band-renormalized shift current (BRSC) --- in monolayer MoS2. We find that the zero-point renormalization alone, without any polarization-carrying photoexcited phonons and with barely any alteration of the band dispersion, dramatically reshapes the SC spectrum: emergent low-energy peaks arise from phonon-assisted optical transitions between momentum-distinct states, with a pronounced redshift of higher-energy features. A mere 1.0% strain sharply tunes the BRSC, whereas raising the temperature enhances it. Our findings overturn the band-structure-only paradigm, establishing electron-phonon coupling as an indispensable ingredient for nonlinear photocurrent and opening a strain-thermal route for engineering next-generation optoelectronic responses.

papers.title: Pressure-Induced Phase Transition and Superconducting Properties of LiPdH$_2$: A First-Principles Study
papers.abstract: We present a detailed first-principles investigation of the superconducting hydride LiPdH$_2$, focusing on the competition between its tetragonal $P4/mmm$ and rhombohedral $R\bar{3}m$ phases. Our results reveal a pressure-induced phase transition near 220 GPa, where $R\bar{3}m$ overtakes $P4/mmm$ in thermodynamic stability. The $R\bar{3}m$ phase is predicted to be superconducting, with $T_{\rm c}$ values of up to 46 K in the harmonic approximation and 28 K at the anharmonic level. In contrast, although the $P4/mmm$ phase is stable up to 200 GPa, it maintains a more rigid electronic character with weaker hydrogen involvement, resulting in lower superconducting performance. Ionic quantum and anharmonic effects play a decisive role in stabilizing $P4/mmm$ and shaping its superconducting properties, whereas these effects diminish rapidly with pressure. These findings highlight the interplay between structural stability, hydrogen orbital activity, and quantum effect in optimizing the superconductivity of hydrogen-based superconductors.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Resolution of Luttinger's Theorem Violations in Strongly Correlated Systems
papers.abstract: Many-body physics faces an apparent paradox concerning violations of Luttinger's theorem in strongly correlated systems. The theorem relates the electron number to the Luttinger count -- the monodromy of the logarithm of the imaginary-frequency Green's function $G(iε)$ -- and, at finite magnetic field, connects the Hall conductivity to the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger count via the Streda formula. Here, we provide a non-perturbative solution to this paradox. We demonstrate that the reported violations of Luttinger's theorem do not require a breakdown of the skeleton diagram representation of physical quantities, thereby resolving a long-standing point of contention in many-body theory. Furthermore, we show that the Luttinger integral, which accounts for the mismatch between the particle number and the Luttinger count, is itself a genuine topological invariant directly tied to the Luttinger-Ward functional $Φ[G]$ rather than to the Green's function alone. We demonstrate that this invariant, like the monodromy of $\ln G(iε)$ itself, stems exclusively from the zero-frequency discontinuity of the Matsubara trajectory.

papers.title: Contrasting fate of holes introduced by Fe or In in kagome metal CoSn
papers.abstract: CoSn is a kagome metal with well-defined flat bands 0.2 eV below the Fermi level EF. Moving them across EF would offer a rare opportunity to investigate their impact on electronic properties. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and X-ray absorption at the Co K-edge, we examine two routes to introduce holes in this compound, through Co/Fe or Sn/In substitutions. Substituting In for Sn produces an almost rigid upward shift of the bands toward EF, as expected for hole doping, whereas substituting Fe for Co leads to an unexpected downward shift. Density functional theory calculations reproduce these opposite trends and trace the unusual behavior of Fe to its local magnetic moment. The moment keeps the hole on the Fe impurity and imposes an attractive electrostatic potential on neighboring Co atoms. Overall, both substitutions bring weakly dispersing states close to EF, the flat bands of the Co kagome lattice upon In substitution and partly localized states around magnetic Fe impurities upon Fe substitution.

papers.title: Anisotropic g-tensor and strong spin-orbit interaction of holes in hexagonal germanium nanowires
papers.abstract: Hexagonal germanium combines direct-gap optical activity with the low-nuclear-spin environment of a group-IV material, making it a candidate platform for spin qubits and spin-photon interfaces. Using a ten-band $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ model, we study the response of confined hole states in hexagonal germanium nanowires to magnetic and electric fields. We show that, by symmetry, the top valence band of the bulk crystal has a vanishing $g$ factor in the plane perpendicular to the $c$ axis, in analogy with the in-plane $g$ factor of heavy holes in two-dimensional hole gases. In nanowires, confinement induces only small transverse $g$-tensor components, so the $g$ tensor remains strongly anisotropic. A transverse electric field strongly reduces the nanowire band gap, providing a gate-tunable optical signature and limiting the usable field range. The same field induces a Rashba spin-orbit interaction that is markedly stronger for fields perpendicular to the $c$ axis and depends nonlinearly on the field strength. In narrow wires at strong fields, the spin-orbit length reaches a few tens of nanometers, comparable to hole devices in cubic silicon. We identify the microscopic origin of the Rashba coupling as a second-order process mediated by a few intermediate subbands with distinct symmetry selection rules. Our results provide guidance for the design of electrically controlled hole-spin qubits in hexagonal germanium nanowires.

papers.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models generate text by reversing a stochastic masking process. Unlike autoregressive LLMs, which generate text one token at a time, they can reveal many tokens in parallel, at the price of an error, since tokens revealed together are drawn independently. We show that this trade-off maps onto the statistical physics of driven many-particle systems. (i) For any data, the error of parallel generation is the entropy production of the generation process relative to the reversed masking process. (ii) For Markov data, generation is a random sequential adsorption process with labelled gaps, which we solve exactly for any number of steps. (iii) For many steps, the error becomes the dissipation of a slowly driven system: the unmasking schedule plays the role of the driving protocol, the number of steps that of its duration, and the error is set by a thermodynamic metric that we obtain in closed form from the mutual information between tokens. Optimal schedules are geodesics of this metric. The exact solution shows how correlations in the text shape both the error and the quality of the output. The longer the correlations, the more the error concentrates at the start of generation. Schedules that start with small steps then gain more, both in path error and in perplexity, and need fewer steps to reach their asymptotic behaviour.

papers.title: Half-integer quantum anomalous Hall effect in MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ via non-magnetic extension
papers.abstract: Within an ab-initio approach, we study the electronic structure and Hall response of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator film of MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ in contact with non-magnetic GeBi$_2$Te$_4$ (Bi$_2$Te$_3$) overlayer. The proposed junction design eliminates the exchange splitting one of the Dirac cones of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ (0001) thus manifesting a half-integer quantum anomalous Hall phase. The described recipe allows to enlarge temperature of the effect observation, enriches the diversity of topological properties of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ compound and is appropriate for other layered antiferromagnetic topological insulators. Applying the proposed heterostructure design, the half-quantized Hall phase can be established with employing other overlayer and magnetic topological insulator films.

papers.title: Signature of chiral anomaly in a graphene-based heterostructure
papers.abstract: Chiral anomaly is a fundamental manifestation of topological matter caused by chirality imbalance. It can be of great practical value by providing a mechanism for dissipationless transport. The phenomenon is highly sensitive to the system dimensionality, disappearing in the 2D limit. Different schemes have been proposed to observe the chiral anomaly in graphene-based systems but experimental evidence has been lacking. Here, we synthesized two types of the Gr/Sr/SiC nanostructure - with 2D and 3D, bulk-like, layers of Sr - the difference being the amount of Sr intercalated under graphene. In contrast to the 2D material, 3D Gr/Sr/SiC exhibits a signature of the chiral anomaly - quadratic negative magnetoresistance in parallel magnetic and electric fields. Also, the functional form of the temperature dependence of the magnetoresistance agrees with the chiral anomaly. In addition, the 3D heterostructure exhibits suppressed conductivity and quantum oscillations in graphene. These effects may be associated with the graphene layer incorporated into a complex 3D heterostructure. Hopefully, the discovered signature of chiral anomaly in the built-in graphene would spur research on the phenomenon in topological nanomaterials.

papers.title: Nonlinear Interaction and Topological Selection Rules in two Skyrmion Merging: Emergence of Skyrmionium Textures
papers.abstract: The nonlinear interaction of closely spaced magnetic skyrmions remains poorly understood, particularly the conditions governing their merger into a single skyrmion or a stable skyrmionium. Here, we investigate the merging dynamics of two Néel skyrmions using analytical modelling and micromagnetic simulations based on Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics. We examine the effects of exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, anisotropy, and magnetostatic energies by varying the initial separation, polarity, winding number, and skyrmion size. Our results reveal a topological selection rule: skyrmions with identical polarity and opposite winding numbers form a stable skyrmionium at intermediate overlap, while all other configurations relax into a single skyrmion. We also identify a critical radius below which the skyrmionium collapses, showing that its formation requires both the appropriate topology and a minimum size. Energy analysis reveals that the transition involves cooperative relaxation of exchange frustration and redistribution of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and magnetostatic energies, leading to a double-domain-wall structure. The resulting skyrmionium exhibits persistent breathing oscillations around an equilibrium radius, confirming its dynamical stability as a metastable state. These findings establish a predictive framework for controlling skyrmion merging and provide design guidelines for engineering skyrmionium textures in chiral magnetic nanostructures.

papers.title: Emergent Symmetry in Constant-Density Flocks
papers.abstract: In two dimensions, the ordered phase of constant-density flocks is described by a single angle field, which makes them arguably the simplest systems with a scale-free ordered phase of collective motion. We show that the equation governing the corresponding Nambu-Goldstone mode, completed with terms previously discarded, possesses on large scales an invariance combining a shear and a Galilean boost. Broken at the bare level, this symmetry is restored at the unique attractive fixed point, and the associated Ward identities fix the scaling exponents exactly, as confirmed numerically.

papers.title: Solvable macroscopic models for populations of type I excitability neurons with Gaussian noise
papers.abstract: The dynamics of type I excitability neurons near the bifurcation point are governed by the model of quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (QIF). The model of QIF subject to white Gaussian noise is abundant in statistical physics, since it not only reasonably reproduces the dynamics of some biological systems but also emerges in the problems of stochastic stability and in quantum mechanics of one-dimensional systems with quenched disorder. We derive the solution for the mean interspike interval of a QIF subject to additive Gaussian noise in terms of analytic functions, from the first passage time problem. On the basis of this solution, we construct analytical expressions for the firing rate and population-mean membrane potential in terms of the real and imaginary parts of a certain universal analytic function. With this function, we generalize theoretical results to heterogeneous populations with Lorentzian-distributed parameters. Implementation of theoretical results is demonstrated and examined for two problems: the interplay between chemical and electrical synapses, and the emergence of effective endogenous noise in sparse inhibitory networks. For the latter case, it is possible to cover the scenarios where the effective noise intensity depends on Lorentzian-distributed parameters, which is not feasible directly with the diffusion approximation.

papers.title: Signature of charge-3e tunneling in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: Cooper pairing is a fundamental aspect of superconductivity and results in charge transport with a basic unit of 2e (e is the electron charge). This basic unit can manifest itself as the denominator in the formula for Shapiro steps of ac Josephson effect-nhf/(2e), where h is the Planck constant, f is the ac frequency and n is an integer. Violation of this standard formula may suggest unconventional physics, such as nhf/4e for charge-4e superconductivity. Here, we report discovery of a new sequence of nhf/3e in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions. The microwave frequency/power, temperature, and current annealing dependences of this exotic sequence consistently point to hf/3e as the unit for Shapiro steps, indicating a Josephson tunneling process involving a trio of electrons (3e). This bunching of an odd number of charges distinguishes itself from well-established superconducting processes, which are carried by composite bosons made of an even number of charges. The unusual observations highlight the important interplay between competing charge orders in twisted bilayer systems.

papers.title: Photoinduced switching of orbital-selective Mott states
papers.abstract: We investigate light-driven inversion of orbital selectivity in a two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model initially in an orbital-selective Mott phase. Using the matrix-product-state we show that tailored pulse excitations drive interorbital charge transfer that nearly reverses the orbital occupations. Single-particle spectral snapshots exhibit changes consistent with an interchange of the localized and itinerant characters of the orbitals. We analyze the relevant one- and two-photon excitation channels and show that chirping around the lower-frequency resonance enhances the transfer. These results establish a microscopic route to reversing orbital selectivity and accessing long-lived nonequilibrium states in multiorbital systems.

papers.title: Ground-state properties of uniaxial magnetic model for antiferromagnetic 1/1 periodic approximants to icosahedral quasicrystals
papers.abstract: The ground-state properties of the uniaxial magnetic model in the 1/1 periodic approximant to the icosahedral quasicrystal with antiferromagnetic interactions for the nearest-neighbor bond $J_1$ and the next-nearest-neighbor bond $J_2$ are analyzed theoretically. By performing numerically-exact calculation, we have determined the ground-state phase diagram for the interaction strength $J_2/J_1$ and the magnetic anisotropy defined within the mirror plane reflecting the effect of the crystalline electric field. We have discovered non-collinear magnetic structures, whose magnetic space groups are identified as the antiferromagnetic orders $I_{\rm P}m'\bar{3}'$ and $R_{\rm R}\bar{3}$ with the magnetic propagation vector $(111)$ as well as the antiferromagnetic orders $Im'm'm'$ and $R\bar{3}'$ with the magnetic propagation vector $(000)$ and the ferrimagnetic orders $Im'm'2$, $I2'2'2$, $P2'/m'$, and $P\bar{1}$. By analyzing each ground state with degeneracy, we have revealed the magnetic as well as topological properties, which are useful to analyze experimental observations of rare-earth-based 1/1 approximants considering the effect of magnetic domains.

papers.title: Universal Phase Locking from Slowly Varying Inhomogeneity in Tunnel-Coupled One-Dimensional Condensates
papers.abstract: The sine-Gordon model can be experimentally realised by tunnel-coupled one-dimensional Bose condensates. However, the experiments show relaxation to a phase-locked state, which conflicts with the predictions of the homogeneous integrable theory. Here we combine the truncated Wigner approximation with an asymptotic analysis, and show that this locking is produced by a slowly varying density profile through a universal mechanism, whereby the relative phase near the density maximum drifts towards zero. We show that this drift is already present in the linearised theory and its timescale is determined by the density curvature alone, while it is independent of the tunnel coupling. Rescaling time by the relaxation time scale collapses the dynamics for different system sizes and density profiles, while non-linearity suppresses the excitation returning from the edges.

papers.title: Majorana corner modes and tunable braiding in an altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure
papers.abstract: Zeeman fields are usually required for realizing and manipulating Majorana corner modes at the cost of suppressed superconducting pairing. Altermagnetism offers a new route toward realizing Majorana corner modes under zero net external magnetic fields. Here we propose a theoretical scheme to host Majorana corner modes in a honeycomb-lattice altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure. In contrast to previous studies on square lattices, altermagnetism yields distinct effective low-energy edge masses on various inequivalent edges of the honeycomb lattice. Within a low-energy edge-theory framework, we establish the conditions under which Majorana corner modes emerge for both bearded and zigzag edge terminations. We further explicitly construct a complete set of Clifford gates by tuning the altermagnetic anisotropy and chemical potential of the heterostructure. Our results provide a promising platform for the realization and manipulation of Majorana corner modes.

papers.title: Reduced Glass Transition Temperature with Preserved Super-Arrhenius Dynamics in Nanoconfined Glass-Forming Nematic
papers.abstract: The molecular dynamics and glass-forming behavior of 4-cyano-3-fluorophenyl 4-butylbenzoate (4CFPB) liquid crystal was investigated by broadband dielectric spectroscopy in anodic aluminum oxide cylindrical nanopores of 35 and 73 nm diameter. The primary $α$-relaxation was analyzed using the Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann (VFT) and Mauro-Yue-Ellison-Gupta-Allan (MYEGA) models. Confinement reduces the glass transition temperature from 217 K in bulk to 208-210 K, while preserving the super-Arrhenius character of the $α$-relaxation and a fragility index of approximately 60. Unlike in previously studied 6 and 8 nm pores, the secondary $β$-relaxation remains detectable, with possible intramolecular contributions examined by density functional theory calculations. Next to the pore-size-dependent changes in molecular dynamics and glass transition temperature, cold crystallization is not observed. These findings highlight the distinct effects of geometrical confinement on molecular relaxation, glass formation, and crystallization kinetics.

papers.title: Initial heat-current decay versus thermal transport at a three-body resonance in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
papers.abstract: We theoretically study kinetic relaxation and heat transport in a dilute one-dimensional spinless Fermi gas near a three-body resonance. The full vacuum amplitude of a finite-range interaction enters the linearized Boltzmann collision operator. The resonance position that maximizes the initial heat-current decay rate lies above the one that minimizes the integrated relaxation time. At higher resonance energies, coupling among momentum moments transfers heat-current weight to a slow mode. A faster initial decay can therefore coexist with slower subsequent relaxation and a larger low-frequency heat response. The dissipative responses at two resonance positions reverse their ordering at least twice as frequency increases. Bounds on the full collision operator confirm both reversals. A fourth-moment distortion exhibits the same separation of relaxation scales and provides a probe through the momentum distribution.

papers.title: Fermi-volume anomaly in quartet condensates
papers.abstract: We investigate the relation between density and Fermi volume in a four-component Fermi system with quartet order. For a regular zero-temperature branch without pair order, we express the correction to the Fermi-volume count in terms of the response of the Luttinger-Ward functional to a phase winding of the quartet source. Its leading term is a weighted difference between four-particle and four-hole states. For a Gaussian vertex and parabolic dispersion, we find that the correction expands the Fermi volume in one dimension and contracts it in three dimensions in the parameter range studied. The sign in two dimensions depends on the momentum cutoff. We solve the one-dimensional Dyson equation at fixed density and compare the counting correction obtained from the Fermi points with that evaluated from the dressed spectra at low temperature. At fixed quartet amplitude and peak normalization of the vertex, the correction depends strongly on the vertex width, whereas the fermionic entropy changes little. We also examine the linear pairing response, which can limit the continuation of the unpaired branch to zero temperature.

papers.title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ revealed by neutron spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Using time-of-flight neutron spectroscopy, we have mapped out the magnetic excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ over a broad range of energies and momenta. The observed well-defined magnon dispersions are quantitatively reproduced by linear spin-wave theory based on a minimal bilinear Hamiltonian that includes Heisenberg exchange interactions up to third-nearest neighbors, interlayer couplings, and a single-ion anisotropy term, with no need to invoke a Kitaev interaction. This finding is consistent with the fact that bromine is lighter than iodine, leading to weaker ligand-mediated spin-orbit coupling in NiBr2 than in NiI2, and consequently a reduced Kitaev interaction. Our results establish NiBr$_2$ as a Heisenberg-dominated van der Waals antiferromagnet and support the view that the ligand spin-orbit coupling governs the strength of the bond-dependent interactions within the NiX$_2$ (X = halogen) family.

papers.title: Multi-Channel Non-Abelian Edge Pumping via Multi-Degeneracy Encircling
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian operations enable sequence-dependent control of light, yet experimental realizations in wave systems have remained confined to local bulk or same-boundary modes and have often required fragile gap-closing degeneracies. Conventional Thouless pumps, meanwhile, support only two-channel edge transfer across a single gap. Here we demonstrate multi-channel non-Abelian edge pumping on a silicon photonic chip by adiabatically encircling multiple band degeneracies in a multi-gap lattice. In a minimal three-band band-triangle, two opposite-charge Weyl points and one zero-charge degeneracy are linked by global band connectivity, yielding both opposite-boundary and same-boundary edge channels. Sequencing these channels produces non-Abelian braiding of three topologically protected edge modes that reside on distinct physical boundaries. The process remains fully gapped and is protected by topological winding rather than by maintained spectral degeneracies. The same band-triangle principle extends systematically to an arbitrary number of channels, establishing a scalable route to collective, sequence-controlled routing of topological states in integrated photonic circuits.

papers.title: Ultrafast Moiré Exciton Dynamics Revealed by Two-Dimensional Coherent Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Moiré superlattices of van der Waals heterostructures confine excitons into discrete energy levels in finite-sized samples, yet their internal relaxation pathways remain obscured by inhomogeneous broadening. Here, using two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (2DCS), we directly resolve seven discrete energy levels of the moiré-confined intralayer $\mathrm{WS}_{2}$ A exciton in an hBN-encapsulated $\mathrm{WS}_{2}/\mathrm{WSe}_{2}$ heterostructure, corresponding to a confinement depth of 57.02 meV. By tracking the population of these levels over picosecond delays, we uncover a two-stage thermalization process: an effective exciton temperature drops from 171.8 to 99.3 K within 1.2 ps through rapid intra-manifold population redistribution, followed by a slower recovery toward quasi-equilibrium mediated by exciton--environment interactions. Kullback--Leibler divergence analysis confirms the progressive transition from a non-equilibrium to a Boltzmann-distributed population. Our results establish state-resolved access to moiré exciton dynamics and provide a foundation for exploring nonequilibrium many-body phenomena in moiré quantum materials.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium orientational bistability of a magnetically-driven slender particle
papers.abstract: Externally driven systems are non-equilibrium but accessible to stationary states. By combining theoretical calculations and particle-based simulations, we investigate the orientational configuration of a transversely-magnetized slender particle in a rotating magnetic field. Our results reveal nonequilibrium orientational bistability in both regimes that the particle rotates synchronously and asynchronously with the field. The relative populations of standing and lying orientations depend strongly on the driving frequency in the synchronous regime, whereas they are primarily controlled by the magnetic field strength in the asynchronous regime. Effective free-energy approximations further capture the principal features of the steady-state orientational distributions in both regimes. Our work aims to give a statistical-thermodynamic description of orientational bistability in magnetically-driven slender particles, paving the way for relevant experimental designs and advanced applications.

papers.title: Chiral-vibration-induced magnetism and circular dichroism in organic molecules
papers.abstract: We investigate the vibrational inverse Faraday effect and transient vibrational circular dichroism in benzene, coronene, and methane at the single-molecule level. We combine density-functional tight-binding calculations with damped normal-mode dynamics. Circularly polarized light excites suitable degenerate infrared-active modes, driving chiral nuclear motion that produces effective magnetic moments. Reversing the pump helicity reverses the vibrational chirality and the sign of the transient dichroic response. These results support a writing-readout scheme in which circularly polarized pumping prepares a chiral vibrational state and transient vibrational circular dichroism probes its handedness. We further examine how molecular symmetry shapes the light-induced chiral response across the three molecular systems. This work provides a valuable platform for exploring all-optical control of magnetism and chiroptical probing at the molecular scale.

papers.title: Interfacial polarity control of anomalous Hall effect in LaCoO3-SrIrO3 heterostructures
papers.abstract: Interfacial polarity in oxide heterostructures can drive robust charge redistribution across the interface, yet its role in tailoring topological transport phenomena like the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) remains largely unexplored. Here, we control the sign of polarity-induced charge in SrIrO3-LaCoO3 interfaces by independently engineering the layer stacking sequence and the atomic termination. In-situ angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy directly confirms the sign reversal of the induced charge in SrIrO3 through the contrasting electronic band shifts between different interfacial configurations. Magneto-transport measurements across a systematic matrix of four distinct heterostructures reveal that the AHE can be cleanly toggled on and off: it emerges exclusively under electron-doped conditions, while remaining suppressed for hole-doped SrIrO3. Our results establish that this response originates from an intrinsic, Berry-curvature-driven mechanism governed by polarity-controlled band filling of SrIrO3. These findings shift interfacial polarity from a passive structural consequence to an active design variable for engineering topological quantum states in oxide heterostructures.

papers.title: Electrical conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium: discretization and effective medium approximation
papers.abstract: The effective conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium is studied within a discretization scheme and the effective-medium approximation (EMA). A square lattice is superimposed on a random isotropic medium; each cell is assigned the conductivity of its majority component, and the cell is replaced by a star of four resistors. Neighboring cells are connected by an equivalent resistor whose conductivity is $σ_1$, $σ_2$, or the harmonic mean $σ_{12}=2σ_1σ_2/(σ_1+σ_2)$, with probabilities $(1-p)^2$, $p^2$, and $2p(1-p)$, respectively. Applying Foster's theorem and the EMA yields a closed equation for the dimensionless effective conductivity $x$ and, after transformation, a cubic equation whose coefficients depend on $p$ and the conductivity ratio $r$. The EMA predictions are compared with direct calculations on a $200\times200$ resistor network with periodic lateral boundary conditions and Dirichlet conditions on the top and bottom. For uncorrelated disorder, good agreement is found. For correlated disorder, when resistor conductivities are assigned according to the discretization rule from the colors of adjacent nodes, significant deviations appear and the percolation-like inflection point shifts to the right of $1/2$. The results question the validity of the correlated-disorder EMA approach and help explain discrepancies previously reported for random nanowire networks.

证据与比较：由Foster定理与EMA得到无量纲有效电导率x的闭合方程并化为系数依赖p与电导率比r的三次方程；与200×200网络（侧向周期、上下Dirichlet条件）直接计算比较，无关联无序吻合良好，关联无序偏差显著且拐点右移。

papers.title: Percolation of discorectangles oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions
papers.abstract: The percolation of finite-thickness elongated objects---discorectangles (stadiums)---oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions is studied, extending recent results for zero-thickness sticks. The angular distribution is the ``Maltese cross'' parametrized by $α$. Based on the known analytic expression for the excluded area of a discorectangle pair, the percolation threshold is estimated by the eigenvalue method. The discorectangle connectivity matrix is represented as the stick matrix plus a rank-1 term determined by the constant part of the excluded area, $C=4lw+πw^{2}$, which gives the approximate relations $λ_{\max}^{\mathrm{DR}}\approxλ_{\max}^{\mathrm{stick}}+C$ and $n_c^{\mathrm{DR}}\approx n_c^{\mathrm{stick}}/(1+C n_c^{\mathrm{stick}})$. Finite thickness shifts the absolute thresholds and affects the first normalization, whereas the second normalization, written through maximum eigenvalues, cancels the additive geometric contribution and preserves only the orientational dependence, explaining the universality of the normalized curves. Monte Carlo simulations of unit-length discorectangles with aspect ratios 8, 16, and 32, various domain sizes, periodic boundary conditions, and union--find scaling analysis confirm the theoretical predictions.

papers.title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
papers.abstract: Quench dynamics offer valuable insights to topological matter, wherein the emergent topological phenomena serve as a dynamic probe to the topology of static Hamiltonians. While such a practice has been widely applied to detect the Abelian band topology or the Euler-class topology of band nodes, little is known regarding the quench dynamics of non-Abelian topological insulators in multiband systems, where the intertwining geometry of all eigenstates necessitates the description of noncommutative topological charges. Here we propose a quench protocol for non-Abelian topological insulators, so that the underlying topology can be systematically probed using dynamic signatures. Specifically, we develop a band-projection scheme to extract the gap-resolved topology from dynamic skyrmions in the emergent quasimomentum--time manifolds of the quench processes. These skyrmions are characterized by a series of gap-resolved dynamic Chern numbers, which enable us to reconstruct the full non-Abelian topology of the post-quench Hamiltonian, including the global non-Abelian topological charge and edge-state patterns under the open-boundary condition. Our proposal offers dynamical access to non-Abelian topology in multiband systems, and can be readily implemented using photons or cold atoms.
