papers.title: Interplay between Spin Stripes and Pairing Crossover in the Bilayer Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: Whether $d$-wave or $s_\pm$-wave pairing prevails in the bilayer nickelate \ce{La3Ni2O7} remains unresolved, and how its observed spin order and magnetic excitations relate to the pairing mechanism is unclear. Here, we use finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a minimal bilayer Hubbard model to investigate pairing competition at strong interlayer coupling, where intralayer and interlayer antiferromagnetic correlations have comparable strengths. We find that spin stripes develop spontaneously with increasing hole doping, accompanied by a crossover of the dominant pairing symmetry from $d$-wave to $s_\pm$-wave. The crossover tracks the changing relative strengths of the spin correlations, with the interlayer correlations overtaking their intralayer counterparts in magnitude. Concomitantly, the dynamical spin structure factor exhibits a momentum-dependent reorganization of the magnetic excitations, consistent with fluctuating spin stripes. Our results identify the structure of spin fluctuations as a key link between spin stripes and pairing competition, offering a minimal-model perspective for understanding \ce{La3Ni2O7}.

papers.title: Ferroelectricity and Peierls transition in MOI$_2$ (M=Ta, Nb): a first-principle analysis
papers.abstract: The van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI$_2$ hosts a polar distortion that is commonly attributed to the Peierls dimerization of its Nb chains. Here we show, using first-principles calculations and a Landau-type energy, that the polar instability is in fact a distinct order parameter that does not stem from the Peierls mode condensation and that three main distinct modes are important in the whole MOI$_2$ family. They are a polar mode $P$, an antipolar mode $η$, and a Peierls mode $δ$, whose stabilities and couplings strongly depend on the nature of the $M$ metal element, as evidenced by the fact that the isostructural, TaOI$_2$ system is not polar while possessing Peirls distortions.

papers.title: Gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave source limited by thermal noise
papers.abstract: Josephson junctions are compact on-chip sources of coherent microwave and terahertz radiation, but conventional radiators couple the emission frequency, output power and dissipation through a single bias voltage. Here we demonstrate a gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave radiator based on a graphene weak link integrated with a separately gated graphene shunt resistor. The bias voltage sets the Josephson frequency, while the local gates tune the Josephson current and the total device resistance, enabling electrostatic control of emitted power at a chosen frequency. The device resolves Josephson harmonics up to fourth order, and its radiation power scales with source current and impedance as expected from a lumped-element circuit model. We further show that the emission linewidth is quantitatively described by Johnson-Nyquist noise at the electron temperature. The linewidth therefore provides an on-chip thermometer under bias, with the resistance-dependent heating captured by a minimal heat-balance model based on Wiedemann-Franz diffusion and electron-phonon coupling.

papers.title: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
papers.abstract: The two-body density matrix (TBDM) of a quantum many-body system provides information about particle correlations, e.g., pairing. In this work, we derive the complete spectrum of the TBDM of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas using its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. We obtain analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for an arbitrary number of particles and identify two different types of eigenstates: collective states, formed by superpositions of paired momentum modes, and single-determinant states. We provide a physical interpretation of this structure, explaining the origin of the different eigenstates and their degeneracies. We further derive an asymptotic expansion for the largest eigenvalue, improving on previous estimates and analytically confirming its linear scaling with the particle number, thereby indicating off-diagonal long-range order. For the high-index collective states, we obtain simpler expressions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors, showing that the eigenvalues decay as $n^{-4}$ and that the eigenvectors become independent of the number of particles. Finally, we discuss the connection between the collective states and an effective description in terms of composite bosons, whose spectral properties suggest a behavior consistent with Tan's contact for interacting bosonic systems.

papers.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
papers.abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$ -- the highest value yet reported for $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.

papers.title: Predictions of superconducting properties from chemical bonding interactions
papers.abstract: The need for rapid estimates of superconducting critical temperatures, Tc s, is becoming increasingly urgent as first-principles and artificial intelligence based methods enable the exploration of ever-larger and more chemically complex materials spaces. In this context, chemical bonding based quantities have emerged as promising descriptors for predicting superconductivity. To date, these approaches have mainly been developed for hydride superconductors, notably through the networking value, a descriptor based upon the electron localization function, whose topological properties have been found to correlate with Tc . In this perspective, we review and consolidate the method's theory, and we discuss how the estimate of the Tc is achievable within a real-space view. We conclude by proposing a framework that enables Tc prediction for the broad family of conventional superconductors from easily computable intermediate physical quantities.

papers.title: Emergent Incompressibility in Polariton Condensates for Scalable XY Spin Simulation
papers.abstract: Driven-dissipative polariton networks offer a powerful analog platform for simulating continuous-spin Hamiltonians. However, their practical scalability is fundamentally limited by amplitude-phase coupling and metastable trapping in highly frustrated energy landscapes. Here, we present an \textit{in situ} dual-enhancement mechanism to address these bottlenecks without requiring external site-specific fine-tuning. First, a renormalization-group analysis based on density rescaling shows that higher-order nonlinear loss drives the condensates toward an incompressible regime, intrinsically suppressing amplitude fluctuations and enforcing phase-only dynamics. For macroscopic XY networks (up to 10,000 spins), this phase-amplitude decoupling yields a more than 50-fold reduction in energy, while simultaneously shrinking the standard deviation by a factor of six. More generally, it restores the extensive scaling of the optimized XY energy with system size. Second, to navigate the rugged, nonconvex energy landscape, we introduce weak Hermitian pulses. When implemented through a multistage protocol, these pulses enable repeated escapes from local minima and drive the system to deeper energy minima. Benchmarking shows an increasing advantage with system size, with the polariton simulator outperforming the classical Monte Carlo-SQP baseline in every sampled macroscopic realization. Our work provides a physical framework for scalable polariton analog computing.

papers.title: Coherence Spreading Law in Quenched Homogeneous Bose Gases
papers.abstract: We investigate nonequilibrium coherence spreading in quenched homogeneous bosonic gases both analytically and numerically. Our ensemble-averaged Gross-Pitaevskii trajectory approach and kinetic analysis confirm the linear-in-time growth of the squared coherence length, and explicitly give the spreading-law dependence on the ratio of initial energy to healing energy. When the ratio is relatively small, the squared coherence length grows at a universal rate determined by the ratio of Planck's constant to the particle mass, insensitive to interaction strength and initial momentum distributions. However, our further calculations uncover fundamental limitations to such universality and establish its phase boundaries governed by low system energies, weak interparticle interactions and many-body integrability. Our theory fully reproduces the key experimental signatures and resolves the puzzle of the dynamical origin of the recently observed universal coherence-spreading speed limit [Nature 647, 608-612 (2025)]. Going beyond existing experimental observations, we provide some testable predictions for ultracold-atom experiments and clarify the conditions for the emergence of universal coherent dynamics in nonequilibrium bosonic many-body systems.

papers.title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
papers.abstract: Shock-induced jetting and recompression are plausible mechanisms for hot spot formation in energetic materials, but remain poorly understood. To this end, we apply all-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a shock-loaded sinusoidal surface asperity in the crystalline explosive HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine) to quantify the roles of shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation in determining the jetting response. Our simulations span a shock pressure interval of $\approx$4-47 GPa, which captures responses in both detonation initiation and steady-state detonation regimes. We find that shock strength and asperity curvature exert strong influence on jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, while feature size and crystallographic orientation play more modest roles. Jet morphology correlates strongly with the HMX ambient-pressure phase diagram and the narrow temperature range associated with its liquid phase. Coherent jets form when focusing and dissipation are sufficient to drive local temperatures above the melting point, while formation of molecular plumes is seemingly connected to jet temperatures exceeding the liquid-vapor transition temperature. Formation of plumes is unlike the jetting responses seen in metals, which typically exhibit liquid phases that are stable over wider temperature intervals. This work proposes a simple hypothesis for the connection between jet morphology and ambient-pressure phase diagrams that can be readily tested in other explosives and metals. It also provides a foundation for ongoing nonreactive and reactive MD simulations of jet impact and recompression to quantify the role played by jets in forming hot spots in HMX-based explosives.

papers.title: Topological localization in unentangled random braids
authors: Pieter Hendrik Willem Van Der Hoek
papers.abstract: In 2015, P. Serna, G. Bunin, and A. Nahum numerically investigated fluctuations in a bunch of unentangled random threads. They showed that fluctuations of an individual thread in a braid are qualitatively different from those of a thread embedded in a medium of fixed parallel lines. In particular, Serna et al. observed a logarithmic increase in the average transverse span, $\left<|x_N|\right>$, of a thread with polymer length, $N$. This behavior highlights the collective nature of topological interactions, in which each polymer fluctuates and constrains the motion of the others. Studying this problem both numerically and analytically, we propose the following interpretation: the logarithmic regime is transient, and sufficiently long polymers exhibit topological localization, where $\left<|x_N|\right>$ approaches a finite limit at $N\to\infty$. Unlike localization induced by quenched external disorder, this phenomenon arises solely from collective topological constraints. We study braids within a locally free approximation and support the localization by analytical investigation of Brownian bridges on the asymptotic Cayley graph of a locally free group. We further conjecture that topologically induced localization emerges as a phase transition: for a small number of threads, $n \sim 2÷5$, the span, $\left<|x_N|\right>$, grows algebraically, with the usual scaling $\left<|x_N|\right>\sim N^{1/4}$ at $N\gg 1$; by contrast, for sufficiently large $n$, each thread in a long braid ($N\gg 1$) asymptotically localizes, approaching $\left<|x_N|\right>\sim \mathrm{const}$.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论为主，辅以数值分析；依据摘要中解析研究与数值研究并列；研究对象：无缠结随机辫（unentangled random braids）中的单根聚合物链
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 对数增长区是暂态的，足够长的聚合物出现拓扑局域化，平均横向展宽在N→∞时趋于有限极限。

证据与比较：摘要给出：在局部自由近似下研究辫，并借助局部自由群渐近Cayley图上Brownian bridge的解析研究支持局域化；还提出n~2÷5时⟨|x_N|⟩~N^{1/4}、n足够大时⟨|x_N|⟩~const的猜想。

english_guide.question: What is the asymptotic fate of the transverse span of a single thread in an unentangled random braid: continued logarithmic growth or a finite limit?

english_guide.novelty: The authors state that this localization, unlike quenched external disorder-induced localization, arises solely from collective topological constraints, and conjecture it emerges as a phase transition.

papers.title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals
papers.abstract: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $σ_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $χ_ν(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,ν}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,χ_ν(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $σ_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论推导结合第一性原理计算，依据为对称性选择定则推导与数值验证；研究对象：具水平镜面σ_h的二维晶体，示例为二维超导体Sc2BCH4及块体MgB2

papers.title: Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$: from disorder through $2\times2$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order to stripe order
papers.abstract: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

papers.title: Medial Model of Elastic Curve Contacts, from Clasps to Knits
papers.abstract: Materials constructed from interlocking and tangled fibers are challenging to model and understand due in part to the complex interplay between fiber shape and contact mechanics. Much of our intuition about contact mechanics comes from the Hertzian description, which is based on interactions between convex bodies. However, fibers often form clasp shapes, which involve saddle-shaped contact surfaces; the ability for two interacting bodies to conform to each other along a saddle surface confounds many existing mechanical contact models. Following an observation that contact surfaces between fibers tend to look like minimal, constant mean-curvature surfaces, we seek to test this hypothesis and provide a direct link to geometric modeling methods. To do this, we leverage the medial axis transformation, which generalizes the notion of a Voronoi tessellation to generating curves and surfaces. Through computational studies on an orthogonal clasp and a simple knit structure, we find that the medial axis transformation provides a reasonable model for contact surfaces between identical curves. We also show that a generalization of the medial axis transformation based on radical Voronoi tessellations can be used to well-approximate contact surfaces between non-identical curves. We apply this ``radical axis transform'' to curves of different radii and demonstrate a trend for surfaces to adopt finite mean curvature. Our results may point the way towards more sophisticated geometric methods for modeling tangles.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：计算研究；基于摘要中computational studies的表述；研究对象：相互接触的弹性曲线，具体为orthogonal clasp与简单knit结构

papers.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
papers.abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections, formation-energy calculations and thermodynamic analysis, and data backup. By packaging this expertise as reusable agent skills, DefectSkills supports consistent workflow execution across agentic AI systems and reproducible defect calculations.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：方法/工具开发；依据是提出结构化提示集，非新实验或新理论；研究对象：半导体与绝缘体中的点缺陷，基于VASP的第一性原理计算流程

papers.title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films
papers.abstract: The thermal conductivities of (001) $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films deposited on $c$-plane sapphire substrates were measured with frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). The thermal conductivity increases from 1.83 $^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$ W/m$\cdot$K to 2.26 $^{+0.35}_{-0.40}$ W/m$\cdot$K as the thicknesses increase from 159 nm to 689 nm. This weak thickness dependence indicates that the majority of the intrinsic phonon mean free paths are smaller than the range of investigated film thicknesses. First-principles-based calculations that include phonon-phonon and phonon-boundary scattering capture this size-dependent behavior and support our experimental observation. Temperature-dependent measurements of a 689 nm film from 293 to 400 K show a decrease in thermal conductivity with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon-phonon scattering. A weaker temperature dependence is observed in a 159 nm film where phonon-boundary scattering becomes more prominent. At comparable film thicknesses, our measured $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ films exhibit lower values of cross-plane thermal conductivity than the other experimentally measured Ga$_2$O$_3$ polymorphs. Our experimental observations are supported by prior predictions, which suggest that the low thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ results from its complex crystal structure, which leads to increased anharmonicity and lower phonon group velocities relative to other polymorphs. Thermal management strategies, such as integration with high-thermal-conductivity substrates, may thus be required to mitigate self-heating for $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$-based electronic devices.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：实验为主，辅以第一性原理计算；依据FDTR测量与计算对照；研究对象：(001) κ-Ga₂O₃薄膜/蓝宝石衬底，厚度159–689 nm
papers.abstract_summary_zh: κ-Ga₂O₃薄膜面外热导率低（1.83–2.26 W/m·K），随厚度弱增、随温度下降，低于其他Ga₂O₃多晶型。

研究问题：κ-Ga₂O₃薄膜面外热导率的厚度与温度依赖如何，其数值相对其他Ga₂O₃多晶型处于什么水平？

english_guide.finding: Cross-plane thermal conductivity of (001) κ-Ga₂O₃ films is low, rising from 1.83 W/m·K at 159 nm to 2.26 W/m·K at 689 nm and decreasing with temperature, lower than other Ga₂O₃ polymorphs at comparable thickness.

papers.title: Bypass Transition via the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect
papers.abstract: Non-Hermitian skin lattices can directionally amplify propagating signals. Here we show that this amplification and nonlinear feedback together drive a bypass transition to self-sustained motion, familiar from shear flows. A finite local excitation can trigger sustained periodic or chaotic motion while the resting state remains linearly stable. We develop a return-map theory that predicts the triggering threshold, its scaling with directional gain, and the instability governing near-critical dynamics. The threshold decreases exponentially with chain length. Weak noise triggers sustained motion as well, with a characteristic ignition length that grows logarithmically as noise weakens at fixed observation time. Our work establishes a skin-effect route to bypass transitions, opening a new avenue for predicting and controlling nonlinear wave dynamics.

证据与比较：摘要给出回归映射理论预测：触发阈值及其随定向增益的标度关系、近临界动力学的失稳机制；阈值随链长指数下降；固定观测时间下弱噪声亦可触发，特征点火长度随噪声减弱对数增长。

papers.title: Classification and Signatures of Dissipative Quantum Hall-Superconductor Junctions
papers.abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. Recent experiments [Gül et al., Phys. Rev. X 12, 021057 (2022)] measured the edge conductance from crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) between counter-propagating FQH edges separated by a narrow superconductor. The observed conductance was small and non-quantized, with two distinct behaviors: some states show temperature-independent conductance, while others show conductance that grows as temperature decreases. We explain these results by dissipation to sub-gap modes in the superconductor and present a phase diagram for the FQH-superconductor junction. We show that for Jain states, temperature-independent non-quantized conductance occurs only in the presence of an integer mode (such as at filling $ν=1\pm\frac{1}{m}$, with odd $m\geq3$) strongly coupled to the dissipative channel. The predicted temperature trends qualitatively agree with the experiment, which shows temperature-independent conductance for $ν=2/3$ and integer states, but not for $ν=1/3$ and $ν=2/5$. We propose comparing $ν=4/3$ and $2/3$ to test the predicted influence of the relative chirality of integer and fractional modes.

papers.title: Resonantly interacting $2e/3$ anyons: a controlled microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity that connects electronic interactions in a lightly doped Laughlin state to the universal physics of a resonantly interacting anyon gas. Using geometric quantization of Laughlin quasiholes, we derive the effective many-body Hamiltonian of dilute charge-$2e/3$ anyons, including their valley structure, dispersion, and statistical and short-range interactions, together with an explicit map between anyon and electron observables. This reduces the dilute many-body problem to a few parameters fixed by data computable from few anyon numerics. In analogy with resonant Fermi and Bose gases, we organize the dilute anyon problem around a two-body binding resonance and its relevant and marginal perturbations. For a three-valley gas of charge-$2e/3$ anyons, we identify a resonance whose long-distance theory is governed by an Aharonov-Casher anyon Hamiltonian whose magnetic field is the statistical Chern-Simons field and whose ground state is exactly solvable. Using the ground state wavefunction, we demonstrate Cooper-pair off-diagonal long-range order directly in electron coordinates and determine the pairing symmetry and vortex-lattice structure. The leading perturbations at the fixed point are a relevant pair detuning and a marginal three-body contact in the valley-singlet channel, which determine the compressibility and sound velocity. A repulsive three-body coupling is marginally irrelevant, allowing the fixed point to control a parametrically broad dilute regime near pair resonance, while attractive three-body interactions instead generate charge-$2e$ trimers. More broadly, our results show that binding thresholds between competing anyon composites host universal resonant regimes that are not captured by the lowest-energy anyon species alone, providing a new setting for controlled theories of anyon matter.

papers.title: Quasicrystals are Functionally Graded Materials
papers.abstract: Quasicrystals exhibit long-range order without translational periodicity, posing challenges to compute their electronic properties. Here we show that a quasicrystal can be represented exactly as a periodic approximant with a spatially graded phason, establishing a connection to functionally graded materials. Building on this connection, we develop a controlled quantum theory of quasicrystals. We derive a state-dependent control parameter governed by the quantum metric of local Bloch states, determining when finite approximations are reliable. We further construct a Hamiltonian that correctly predicts Bragg gap positions, quasimomentum equivalence, and quasiperiodic eigenstates to all orders in phason strain within a finite Fourier window. We verify the theory numerically and propose a diffraction-based experimental test of the gap shift induced by phason strain. Our framework opens a route to predicting the electronic structure and functional properties of quasicrystals using methods developed for functionally graded materials.

papers.title: Shapiro spikes in driven quantum fluids
papers.abstract: Periodic driving of a Josephson junction produces resonant transport signatures known as Shapiro spikes, conventionally described by effective circuit models. Here, we demonstrate Shapiro spikes in a neutral quantum fluid using simulations of a potential-biased atomic Josephson junction. The dc-current resonances follow the expected Bessel-function scaling, including the suppression and revival of individual resonances with increasing modulation strength. We uncover their microscopic mechanism by showing that the phase-winding frequency develops finite plateaus at integer multiples of the drive frequency. These phase-locked states are sustained by quantized-vortex nucleation and the associated $2π$ phase slips. Remarkably, within a locking plateau, the dc current and density transfer can reverse direction while the phase-winding frequency remains locked to the drive, giving rise to negative-mobility transport. Our results establish a microscopic link between vortex-mediated phase slips, Shapiro resonances, and anomalous transport in a neutral quantum fluid, revealing how quantized vortices convert resonant transport into phase-locked dynamics with negative mobility.

papers.title: Odd Capillarity
papers.abstract: Capillarity governs interfacial relaxation and hydrodynamic motion in binary fluids through parity-even mechanical stresses. Here, we introduce \emph{odd capillarity}, a parity-breaking interfacial mechanical response, by incorporating a symmetric, nonvariational, parity-odd capillary stress into the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes (CHNS) equations. This stress generates forces along interfaces, transverse to ordinary capillary forces, and performs mechanical work that is not balanced by changes in the composition free energy. Direct numerical simulations reveal that odd capillarity arrests domain coarsening while sustaining turbulent fluid motion without a conventional inertial energy cascade, as energy injection is predominantly balanced by viscous dissipation. In asymmetric mixtures, odd capillarity driven deformation and breakup interrupt droplet growth, producing dynamically arrested emulsions with composition hyperuniformity and suppressed large-scale vorticity fluctuations. These findings establish odd capillarity as a distinct interfacial mechanism for controlling phase separation and sustaining nonequilibrium fluid motion.

papers.title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
papers.abstract: Chiral gauge theories underlie the Standard Model, yet none has been simulated nonperturbatively. Lattice constructions that evade the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces. Here we provide a gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields, in which the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly survive exactly mod $N$. Anomaly cancellation on the lattice lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Using infinite matrix product states, we simulate the canonical 1+1-dimensional chiral gauge theory, the 34-50 model, and find excellent agreement with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at $N=6$ reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model. This provides an efficient and practical solution to the problem of simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, both on classical and quantum computers.

papers.method_zh: 构建基于clock-and-shift qudit与Z_N规范场的规范不变哈密顿量格点正则化，利用格点反常抵消精确求解Gauss定律，再用无限矩阵乘积态模拟。

english_guide.finding: A gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with Z_N gauge fields preserves the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly exactly mod N; anomaly cancellation lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Infinite matrix product state simulations of the 34-50 model agree excellently with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at N=6 reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model.
english_guide.question: How can chiral gauge theories be simulated nonperturbatively, given that lattice constructions evading the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces?
english_guide.evidence: Exact mod N survival of global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly; exact imposition and solution of Gauss laws via lattice anomaly cancellation; infinite matrix product state simulations of the 34-50 model showing excellent agreement with analytic predictions at N=6.
english_guide.method: Gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization using clock-and-shift qudits with Z_N gauge fields; exact solution of Gauss laws; infinite matrix product states.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state an efficient and practical solution to simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, on both classical and quantum computers.
english_guide.limitations: Only 1+1-dimensional abelian theories are addressed; extensions to higher dimensions and non-abelian theories are not stated; quantitative error bounds for the N=6 infrared reproduction are not given in the abstract.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称该方案为1+1维一般阿贝尔手征规范理论提供了高效实用的模拟途径，经典与量子计算机均适用。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要仅涉及1+1维阿贝尔情形；高维与非阿贝尔推广未说明；N=6重现红外物理的适用范围及误差未在摘要中量化。

papers.title: Experimental evaluation of Kolmogorov's first similarity hypothesis for shear-dependent viscosity fluids
papers.abstract: We experimentally investigate the applicability of Kolmogorov's first similarity hypothesis to shear-dependent viscosity fluids. We assess whether dissipative range statistics exhibit a self-similar behavior in nearly homogeneous and isotropic turbulence, using stereo particle image velocimetry in aqueous Carbopol solutions across two concentrations and a range of forcing conditions. We observe that, when normalized by the mean viscosity and mean dissipation rate, second- and third-order structure functions collapse across the different experimental conditions and exhibit functional forms compatible with classical Newtonian results. These observations are in general agreement with the recent numerical results of Rosti [J. Fluid Mech. 1012, R5 (2025)], who proposed that Kolmogorov's similarity hypotheses can be extended to shear-thinning fluids by considering dissipation scales based on the mean viscosity, the mean dissipation rate, and the flow index.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：实验研究；依据为立体粒子图像测速测量；研究对象：近均匀各向同性湍流中的剪切依赖黏性流体（Carbopol水溶液，两种浓度）
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 用平均黏度和平均耗散率归一化后，二阶与三阶结构函数在不同实验条件下塌缩，函数形式与经典牛顿流体结果相容。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：Kolmogorov第一相似假设是否适用于剪切依赖黏性流体的耗散区统计，即耗散区统计是否呈自相似行为。
证据与比较：在两种Carbopol浓度及一系列强迫条件下，用立体粒子图像测速获得二阶、三阶结构函数；以平均黏度和平均耗散率归一化后，不同实验条件间出现塌缩，且函数形式与经典牛顿流体结果相容。
papers.method_zh: 对Carbopol水溶液开展近均匀各向同性湍流实验，采用立体粒子图像测速测量速度场并计算二阶、三阶结构函数。

english_guide.finding: When normalized by mean viscosity and mean dissipation rate, second- and third-order structure functions collapse across conditions and show functional forms compatible with classical Newtonian results.
english_guide.question: Whether Kolmogorov's first similarity hypothesis applies to shear-dependent viscosity fluids, i.e., whether dissipative-range statistics are self-similar.
english_guide.evidence: Stereo particle image velocimetry in aqueous Carbopol solutions at two concentrations and a range of forcing conditions; normalized second- and third-order structure functions collapse across conditions and are compatible with Newtonian forms.
english_guide.method: Nearly homogeneous and isotropic turbulence experiments in aqueous Carbopol solutions using stereo particle image velocimetry, with second- and third-order structure functions computed.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state general agreement with Rosti (2025), who proposed extending Kolmogorov's similarity hypotheses to shear-thinning fluids using dissipation scales based on mean viscosity, mean dissipation rate, and flow index.
english_guide.limitations: Abstract covers only aqueous Carbopol solutions at two concentrations under nearly homogeneous and isotropic turbulence; parameter ranges, uncertainty analysis, and applicability to non-homogeneous or anisotropic cases are not specified.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称实验观测与Rosti（2025）的数值结果总体一致，后者提出以平均黏度、平均耗散率和流动指数定义耗散尺度，可将Kolmogorov相似假设推广至剪切变稀流体。

papers.title: A local Yang-Baxter obstruction for the hard-square model
papers.abstract: Many exact solutions of two-dimensional lattice models rest on an analytic family of weights satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation. The hard-hexagon model was solved in this way, while the neighbouring hard-square model has no known closed form. We determine the height alphabets that encode hard squares without hidden heights, and there are exactly two connected ones, the occupation variables themselves and the four heights of Andrews, Baxter and Forrester. Hard hexagons is integrable on both, but no analytic Yang-Baxter family of face weights passes through hard squares at nonzero activity on either. The difference lies in the exclusion rule, which for hard squares turns a few Yang-Baxter equations into polynomial identities that force auxiliary weights to vanish. A closed form for hard squares is not excluded, but a solution by this route would have to leave these encodings or go beyond a single analytic family through the model. Encodings with hidden heights remain open.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论；基于Yang-Baxter方程与面权重分析的严格推导；研究对象：hard-square model（硬方块模型）及其高度字母表编码，对照hard-hexagon model（硬六边形模型）
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 在无非隐藏高度的两种连通高度编码下，非零活度处均不存在经过hard squares的解析Yang-Baxter面权重族。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：hard squares能否像hard hexagons那样，通过某个解析Yang-Baxter权重族获得精确解？
证据与比较：摘要给出：无非隐藏高度且连通的编码恰有两种，即占据变量本身与Andrews-Baxter-Forrester四高度；hard hexagons在两者上可积，而hard squares在非零活度下均无解析Yang-Baxter面权重族通过。
papers.method_zh: 确定hard squares的高度字母表编码，并检验面权重Yang-Baxter方程；将排除规则导致的方程化为迫使辅助权重为零的多项式恒等式。

english_guide.finding: Under the two connected height encodings without hidden heights, no analytic Yang-Baxter family of face weights passes through hard squares at nonzero activity.
english_guide.question: Can hard squares be solved exactly through an analytic Yang-Baxter family, as hard hexagons were?
english_guide.evidence: Exactly two connected encodings without hidden heights exist: the occupation variables and the four Andrews-Baxter-Forrester heights. Hard hexagons is integrable on both, but hard squares admits no such analytic Yang-Baxter family at nonzero activity on either.
english_guide.method: Determine height alphabets encoding hard squares and test the face-weight Yang-Baxter equations; the exclusion rule turns a few equations into polynomial identities forcing auxiliary weights to vanish.
english_guide.novelty: The authors report a local Yang-Baxter obstruction for hard squares: no analytic Yang-Baxter family passes through nonzero activity in either connected encoding.
english_guide.limitations: A closed form for hard squares is not excluded; such a solution would have to leave these encodings or go beyond a single analytic family. Encodings with hidden heights remain open.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称给出hard squares的局部Yang-Baxter障碍：两种连通编码下均无解析Yang-Baxter族通过非零活度点。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未排除hard squares存在闭式解；该路线需离开这些编码或超越单一解析族；含隐藏高度的编码仍未解决。

papers.title: How Rich is the Rich-Club? Super Rich-Club Organization in Complex Networks
papers.abstract: The rich-club coefficient is used in complex networks to quantify the tendency of progressively higher-degree nodes to be more densely connected than expected by chance. However, it does not capture whether high degree nodes towards the core are actually more interconnected than the original network. Here, we jointly analyze the rich-club coefficient and an enrichment coefficient, which quantifies whether the internal average degree of progressively higher-degree subgraphs is greater than that of the original network, despite the decreasing number of nodes. We apply this framework to real and synthetic networks. Our results reveal three distinct regimes of core organization: rich-club organization without enrichment, enrichment without rich-club organization, and a combination of both, which we call Super Rich-Club organization. In the latter regime, high-degree nodes form cohesive and unusually dense cores that support efficient communication. Our results show that characterizing core organization across structural scales requires considering both relative density and internal connectivity, revealing a stronger form of core organization in real systems with implications for network structure, spectral properties that govern dynamical processes, and communicability.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论/计算；基于真实与合成网络的联合分析；研究对象：复杂网络的高阶节点核心组织，真实网络与合成网络
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 结合 rich-club coefficient 与 enrichment coefficient 可区分三种核心组织模式，其中二者兼具的 Super Rich-Club organization 表现为高阶节点形成内聚且异常致密的核心。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：rich-club coefficient 只衡量高阶节点连接是否高于随机预期，无法判断趋向核心的高阶节点是否比原网络更互联；如何刻画跨结构尺度的核心组织？
证据与比较：摘要称对真实与合成网络联合应用 rich-club coefficient 与 enrichment coefficient，识别出三种模式：有 rich-club 无 enrichment、有 enrichment 无 rich-club、二者兼具；并称 Super Rich-Club 核心支持高效通信。未给出具体网络数量或定量数值。
papers.method_zh: 联合分析 rich-club coefficient 与 enrichment coefficient，后者量化逐级高阶子图内部平均度是否高于原网络，并应用于真实与合成网络。

english_guide.finding: Jointly analyzing the rich-club coefficient and an enrichment coefficient reveals three regimes of core organization: rich-club without enrichment, enrichment without rich-club, and Super Rich-Club organization, in which high-degree nodes form cohesive, unusually dense cores supporting efficient communication.
english_guide.question: The rich-club coefficient does not capture whether high-degree nodes towards the core are actually more interconnected than the original network; how can core organization be characterized across structural scales?
english_guide.evidence: The framework is applied to real and synthetic networks, identifying three regimes; Super Rich-Club cores are described as cohesive and unusually dense and as supporting efficient communication. No specific network counts or quantitative values are given in the abstract.
english_guide.method: Joint analysis of the rich-club coefficient and an enrichment coefficient quantifying whether the internal average degree of progressively higher-degree subgraphs exceeds that of the original network, applied to real and synthetic networks.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state that characterizing core organization across structural scales requires considering both relative density and internal connectivity, revealing a stronger form of core organization termed Super Rich-Club organization.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify the network list, scales, statistical significance, or applicability conditions; the RSS excerpt may be truncated and the full text was not read, so quantitative details cannot be verified.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称需同时考虑相对密度与内部连通性来刻画跨结构尺度的核心组织，并提出 Super Rich-Club organization 这一更强核心组织形式。

papers.title: Photonic and Electronic Interaction of TMD-Hybridized ZnO Nanowire Lasers
papers.abstract: Semiconductor nanowire lasers are promising on-chip coherent light sources for photonic integrated circuits, but integration inevitably places them in contact with other materials, thereby changing their properties upon hybridization. In this study, we examine the photonic and electronic coupling between single ZnO nanowire lasers and TMDs. Using deterministic nanomanipulation, we first hybridized the same nanowire first with a WS$_2$ monolayer and then with a MoS$_2$ monolayer. The respective lasing threshold rises, the emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS$_2$, lasing is fully suppressed. Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations show that the TMD absorbs part of the evanescent field. Because this absorption is wavelength dependent, it also removes modes from the low-energy flank of the envelope, which accounts for small difference between the two monolayers, while the blueshift itself follows the increase of the carrier density at threshold. Density functional theory calculations that include the interface dipole predict a type-I alignment at the ideal ZnO(10$\bar{1}$0)/TMD interface, which turns into type~II for a moderately reduced dipole, as expected for hydroxylated facets in air. In both cases, holes are transferred from the nanowire into the TMD and removed from the gain medium. Evanescent absorption and hole transfer thus jointly suppress lasing, and both must be accounted for when integrating nanowire lasers with 2D materials.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：实验与计算混合；同一纳米线顺序杂化并辅以模拟；研究对象：单根ZnO纳米线与WS₂、MoS₂单层及多层MoS₂的杂化体系
papers.abstract_summary_zh: TMD对倏逝场的吸收与空穴转移共同抑制ZnO纳米线激光，二者在集成时都需考虑。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：ZnO纳米线激光器与TMD杂化后，光子与电子耦合如何改变激光阈值、发射强度与模式包络？
证据与比较：同一纳米线依次与WS₂、MoS₂单层杂化后阈值升高、高泵浦功率密度下发射强烈猝灭、模式包络蓝移；与双层、三层及体MoS₂杂化后激光完全被抑制。
papers.method_zh: 确定性纳米操纵实现杂化；有限差分本征模模拟倏逝场吸收；含界面偶极的密度泛函理论计算能带对齐。

english_guide.finding: Evanescent absorption by the TMD and hole transfer from the ZnO nanowire jointly suppress lasing, and both must be accounted for when integrating nanowire lasers with 2D materials.
english_guide.question: How do photonic and electronic coupling between a single ZnO nanowire laser and TMDs alter the lasing threshold, emission intensity, and mode envelope upon hybridization?
english_guide.evidence: The same nanowire was hybridized first with a WS2 monolayer and then with a MoS2 monolayer; the lasing threshold rises, emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS2, lasing is fully suppressed.
english_guide.method: Deterministic nanomanipulation; Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations showing wavelength-dependent TMD absorption of part of the evanescent field; density functional theory calculations including the interface dipole predicting type-I alignment at the ideal ZnO(10-10)/TMD interface, turning into type II for a moderately reduced dipole.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state that the same nanowire was hybridized first with a WS2 monolayer and then with a MoS2 monolayer, and that evanescent absorption and hole transfer jointly suppress lasing.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify environmental conditions, quantitative threshold values, or the specific interface dipole magnitude; conclusions are based on the systems described in the abstract.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称在同一纳米线上顺序杂化不同TMD，并将倏逝吸收与空穴转移共同归为激光抑制机制。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明环境条件、定量阈值数值及界面偶极具体取值；结论基于摘要所述体系。

papers.title: Cryogenic suppression of correlated loss in Rydberg atom arrays
papers.abstract: Blackbody radiation (BBR) poses a central challenge for quantum science with Rydberg atoms. By driving transitions to nearby opposite-parity states, BBR shortens Rydberg lifetimes and has long been suspected to trigger "avalanche" events known to cause correlated atom loss. Here, we suppress avalanche decay and establish BBR as its dominant trigger using a Rydberg atom array that operates either cryogenically or at room temperature. A $45~\text{K}$ radiation shield reduces ambient BBR, extending Rydberg $nS$ lifetimes for $n$ ranging from 50 to 75. BBR-induced decay rates are suppressed by 30%-50%, corresponding to an effective blackbody temperature $T_{\rm eff}\approx190~\text{K}$. This enables controlled comparisons of Rydberg-dressed atom arrays operating in different BBR environments. Arrays of up to 70 atoms demonstrate cryogenically suppressed avalanche rates, tracking the suppression in BBR-induced decay, for both $n=50$ and $n=60$ dressing. A parameter-free rate model agrees with the measured avalanche rates after accounting for frequency-dependent cryogenic shielding, photoionization-triggered avalanches, laser phase noise, BBR decay channels, and Rydberg interaction effects. We demonstrate a quantitative description of avalanche decay and show that improved BBR shielding should further suppress correlated loss to the $T_\text{eff}=45~\text{K}$ achievable in the current apparatus. Our results establish a route to mitigating correlated errors that otherwise impede fault-tolerant operation in neutral-atom quantum processors.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：实验；对比低温与室温装置并配合速率模型；研究对象：里德堡原子阵列（Rydberg atom arrays），nS 态 n=50–75，最多70个原子
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 45 K辐射屏蔽降低环境黑体辐射，使里德堡nS态寿命延长、BBR诱导衰减率降低30%–50%，并相应抑制雪崩型关联原子损失。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：黑体辐射是否为里德堡原子阵列中关联原子损失（雪崩衰减）的主导触发因素，低温屏蔽能否抑制该损失。
证据与比较：低温与室温装置对比：45 K屏蔽下n=50–75的nS寿命延长，BBR诱导衰减率降低30%–50%，对应有效黑体温度约190 K；n=50和n=60缀饰下最多70原子阵列的雪崩率随BBR衰减同步受抑；无自由参数速率模型与实测雪崩率一致。
papers.method_zh: 在可低温或室温运行的里德堡原子阵列中对比测量，并用计入频率相关屏蔽、光电离触发雪崩、激光相位噪声、BBR衰减通道和里德堡相互作用的无自由参数速率模型分析。

english_guide.finding: A 45 K radiation shield suppresses blackbody-radiation-induced decay rates by 30%-50%, corresponding to an effective blackbody temperature Teff of about 190 K, and cryogenically suppresses avalanche rates in Rydberg atom arrays of up to 70 atoms for n=50 and n=60 dressing.
english_guide.question: Whether blackbody radiation is the dominant trigger of correlated atom loss via avalanche decay in Rydberg atom arrays, and whether cryogenic shielding can suppress it.
english_guide.evidence: Cryogenic versus room-temperature operation; extended Rydberg nS lifetimes for n=50-75; 30%-50% suppression of BBR-induced decay; avalanche rates tracking BBR suppression for n=50 and n=60; a parameter-free rate model agreeing with measured avalanche rates.
english_guide.method: Rydberg atom arrays operating cryogenically or at room temperature, with a parameter-free rate model accounting for frequency-dependent cryogenic shielding, photoionization-triggered avalanches, laser phase noise, BBR decay channels, and Rydberg interaction effects.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state that they suppress avalanche decay and establish BBR as its dominant trigger, provide a quantitative description of avalanche decay, and show improved shielding should further suppress correlated loss to Teff=45 K achievable in the current apparatus.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify atomic species, array geometry, temperature-control details, or statistical uncertainties; conclusions are limited to measured nS states with n=50-75 and arrays of up to 70 atoms, and Teff=45 K is projected rather than measured.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称通过抑制雪崩衰减并确立BBR为其主导触发因素，实现了对雪崩衰减的定量描述，并指出改进屏蔽可将关联损失进一步降至当前装置可达的Teff=45 K。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明原子种类、阵列几何、温度控制细节及统计不确定度；结论限于所测n=50–75的nS态与最多70原子阵列，Teff=45 K为预期而非已实测。

papers.title: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation
papers.abstract: Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. Overall, this work provides a experimentally verifiable phenomenological description for the dynamics of quantum fluids and demonstrates the applicability of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation in characterizing such systems.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论研究；从NFPE推导涨落流体力学；研究对象：量子流体：理想费米气体与玻色流体
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 由非线性Fokker-Planck方程建立量子流体涨落流体力学，并给出相应随机热力学与涨落定理。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：如何从非线性Fokker-Planck方程出发，为量子流体构建可实验检验的涨落流体力学与随机热力学描述？
证据与比较：摘要给出两类应用：理想费米气体中电阻正比于温度与费米面态密度之积；玻色流体中临界慢化弛豫时间呈三种标度行为，分别对应无相互作用、排斥相互作用与吸引相互作用区域。
papers.method_zh: 以非线性Fokker-Planck方程（NFPE）为起点推导涨落流体力学，并建立随机热力学与涨落定理。

english_guide.finding: Fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids is established from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), with stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems derived.
english_guide.question: How can fluctuating hydrodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics for quantum fluids be constructed from the NFPE?
english_guide.evidence: For the ideal Fermi gas, resistance is proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface; for bosonic fluids, the relaxation time shows three scaling behaviors for non-interacting, repulsive, and attractive interaction regimes.
english_guide.method: Derivation starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), including stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state the work provides an experimentally verifiable phenomenological description of quantum fluid dynamics and demonstrates the applicability of the NFPE.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify interaction strength, temperature range, or dimensionality; experimental verification details are not provided.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称本工作为量子流体动力学提供可实验验证的唯象描述，并展示NFPE刻画此类系统的适用性。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明相互作用强度、温度范围与维度等适用条件；结论基于理论推导，摘要未给出实验验证细节。

papers.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
papers.abstract: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).

papers.title: Helium States in a CAS(2,2) Subspace Inspired by Quantum Photonics
papers.abstract: We present a four-mode Fock-state photonics implementation of the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm to calculate the ground-state and excited-state energies for the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) Subspace. Its CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock-space representation and subsequently optimized using a continuous-variable quantum circuit. The circuit architecture under study is constructed of single-mode phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. The variational circuit is initialized in the Fock state $\ket{1100}$ and its performance is benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) Hamiltonian. We also extend the method to optimize from the first to three excited states of the helium atom with the aid of the variational quantum deflation $(VQD)$ method in a CAS(2,2). We then investigate the performance of this circuit architecture as a basis for implementing the VQD method. In the ideal noiseless simulation setting, we see that the survival probability of the ground and the excited states within the target $CAS$ subspace is unity, because the total photon number and the photon number in the two spin sectors $α$ and $β$ are preserved. We demonstrate that the proposed approach enables the determination of the ground and excited-state energies within the CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space using a continuous-variable quantum circuit and the variational quantum deflation ($VQD$) algorithm, while satisfying the orthogonality conditions with negligible errors.

papers.title: Directional Control of Chiral Polymer Emission Dissymmetry by Plasmonic Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Circularly polarized (CP) emission is central to next-generation photonic and optoelectronic technologies, yet simultaneously controlling its directionality, intensity, and handedness remains a major challenge. Advances in molecular and materials design have enabled strong chiral light-matter interactions and large dissymmetry between opposite CP states. However, conventional thin-film architectures provide limited control over the angular distribution of CP emission and often exhibit strongly angle-dependent chiral emission. Metasurfaces, on the other hand, offer powerful control over emission directionality and polarization, but have predominantly been explored with intrinsically achiral emitters. For the first time, we integrate organic chiral polymer thin films with planar chiral plasmonic metasurfaces to enhance chiral light-matter interactions while controlling the directionality and angular dependence of chiral emission. Using angle-resolved Stokes Fourier polarimetry, we show that metasurface coupling produces directional emission, near-normal dissymmetry factors exceeding 0.7, and, remarkably, direction-dependent reversal of the emission handedness at fixed molecular stereochemistry.

papers.title: Discrete Backbone Elasticity and Curvature-Dependent Torsion Statistics in Proteins
papers.abstract: Coarse-grained models of protein conformational dynamics use $\mathrm{C}_α$ geometry to describe the probabilities of regular helices, ordered turns and disordered conformations. To test how much of this order arises from local chain elasticity, we connect discrete Hasimoto frame transport to neighboring bending mismatch, deriving a curvature-product torsion interaction and a six-parameter generalized von Mises density. Fitted on 194 chains from the ATLAS molecular dynamics database and tested on 1744 sequence-nonredundant proteins, this baseline reduces negative log-density loss from 1.490 to 1.160 nats, torsion-sign error from 12.26 to 2.15 percentage points, and helix-fraction error from 21.84 to 10.41 points. Ablations and circular-moment projections against reference generative models motivate extensions to anisotropic stiffness and two partition-function-weighted elastic states, further lowering test loss to 0.790 nats and helix error to 1.65 points. The fixed hierarchy also improves predictions across 72 trajectories of peptides $\mathrm{Fs}$ and $(\mathrm{AAQAA})_3$ and miniprotein $\mathrm{HP35}$ spanning varied starting conformations and force fields. Remaining angular errors in these trajectories are associated with atomic context at shared bends, as bend-matched peptide frames adopt opposite torsion signs with distinct hydrogen-bond patterns and a proline-containing $\mathrm{HP35}$ turn remains at negative torsion. Introducing a bilinearly coupled $\mathrm{C}_α$--$\mathrm{N}$ orientation angle largely reparameterizes the existing bend-dependent harmonics, with an empirical $L^2$ Gram projection placing 96.7\% to 99.6\% of its added coefficient-function squared norm within the original six-function span. These results link discrete Hasimoto elasticity to statistical backbone potentials and clarify the scope and limits of local $\mathrm{C}_α$ geometry.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Nanocavities for Single-Molecule Vibrational Strong Coupling
papers.abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in low-loss anisotropic materials such as hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) provide extreme sub-diffractional field confinement in the mid-infrared, making them attractive for enhancing the interaction of light with molecular vibrations. Collective vibrational strong coupling between molecular ensembles and HPhPs has already been demonstrated in extended slabs. Reaching this regime with a single molecule, however, remains a major challenge, and would provide a platform for investigating how vacuum electromagnetic fields influence molecular dynamics and chemical reactivity. Here, we show theoretically that single-molecule vibrational strong coupling can be reached in hBN nanocavities that laterally confine HPhPs within a finite volume. Combining full-wave electromagnetic simulations with the few-mode quantization approach, we find that these nanocavities support a rich set of asymmetric resonances that strongly enhance the local spectral density, with frequencies that follow from simple HPhP ray trajectories and can be tuned through the cavity aspect ratio. We identify resonances with quality factors of about $600$ and effective mode volumes of $|V_{\mathrm{eff}}| \sim 10^{-7}λ^{3}$, sufficient for single-molecule strong coupling with vibrational transitions with dipole moments on the order of $1\,\mathrm{D}$. These results establish hyperbolic nanocavities as a promising platform for single-molecule vibrational strong coupling and open new routes toward the local control of vibrational dynamics and molecular energy flow.

papers.title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
papers.abstract: Vanishing-error recovery of a fusion qubit from a fixed-sector ground doublet of four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain requires at least the shorter three-defect span of physical spins to leading order. Across arbitrary preselected spin sets and unrestricted joint decoding, this bound holds when the thermodynamic limit precedes large spacings at fixed positive ratios. An exact interval decoder attains it. Collective records of both logical axes in the complement force successful near-minimal supports to concentrate in density on a leading-order shortest interval.

papers.title: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization
papers.abstract: Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through the transport-information correspondence, the UCN quantify the information-theoretic cost due to discretization as the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions associated with the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we introduce an alternative local-map discretization scheme in which the probability mass within each cell is transported to its own probability-weighted centroid. This change in the representative-point selection enables an exact expression for the transport cost of each cell in terms of the covariance matrix of its conditional probability distribution and the Fisher metric of the underlying continuous family. We establish an exact correspondence between the resulting transport cost and the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus generalizes the transport-information correspondence to finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded convex sets.

papers.title: Rotated-Frame Determinant Discovery for Ground- and Excited-State Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction
papers.abstract: Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI) constructs a variational determinant space from measurements of a prepared electronic state, but finite-shot sampling can repeatedly observe high-probability determinants, limiting efficient discovery of configurations important for an accurate selected-CI description. We introduce rotate--sample--unrotate (RSU) determinant discovery, in which the same state is sampled in complementary orbital frames and the observed rotated determinants generate a finite set of candidates in the canonical basis. The Hamiltonian is then diagonalized in an orthonormal selected-CI space without enumerating the full determinant space. State-targeted orbital frames are constructed from an initial selected-CI wavefunction and its external residual. For excited states, we combine RSU with the generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) to prepare target-specific sampling states. Candidate GQE circuits are evaluated by classical selected-CI diagonalization in finite sampled spaces, so the quantum procedure requires only state preparation and determinant sampling. For N$_2$, exact-state controls isolate the determinant-discovery effect: at the stretched geometry, residual-natural-orbital RSU reaches chemical accuracy with 5,000 shots, compared with 20,000 shots for conventional QSCI. The improvement persists with approximate GQE-prepared states and is also observed for target excited states. These results demonstrate improved finite-shot determinant discovery in QSCI for both ground and excited states.

papers.title: Dynamical Signatures of Selective Gap Closing in Multi-Dimensional Monotone Quasiperiodic Operators
papers.abstract: We translate the spectral gap-closing criterion for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators into a concrete dynamical protocol and verify it by large-scale numerics. For a non-principal label we construct a sampling function whose leading eigenfunction weight at the origin vanishes; a local bump then drives the residual weight through zero. The height of a weighted oscillatory time average of the origin-to-localization-center correlator exhibits a deep minimum precisely at the closing, while the site-control label remains featureless and orders of magnitude larger. The signature is robust and maps directly onto superconducting-circuit and photonic platforms.

papers.title: Chiral edge modes from lattice Chern-Simons theory
papers.abstract: It is shown that a level $k$ Abelian lattice Chern-Simons theory with continuum time and a spatial square lattice, which is a topological field theory on the latticized plane and torus, when quantized on a spatial cylinder reduces to chiral edge excitations, exactly localized on the two boundaries and carrying two commuting lattice versions of the level-$k$ $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra of opposite chirality. The algebras are represented on a Fock space in the noncompact theory and by a finite Weyl algebra in the compact one. We also observe that the theory has a natural framing of Wilson loops which exhibits the correct framing anomaly.

papers.title: Raychaudhuri-Ehlers Kinematics on Quantum State-Space: Caustics and Extrinsic Quantum Geometry
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics is inherently geometric in that the pure states form a curved complex manifold and the Schrödinger evolution defines a Hamiltonian flow on this space. Geometry identifies constraints on flows on quantum state-space that hold independently of their microscopic realization. We uncover such universal behavior in families of geodesic paths on the quantum state-space using the Raychaudhuri-Ehlers equations. We show that the complex structure leads to tidal anisotropy in the curvature, and for Hilbert space dimension $N\geq3$, complete point-emitted geodesic bundles necessarily develop shear and undergo direction-selective focusing at finite distance. We give these geometric results an information-theoretic interpretation in terms of fidelity susceptibility and quantum Fisher information. For ground-state manifolds constrained by physical parameters, we resolve the tidal curvature into Berry-curvature-dependent ambient tides and contributions from extrinsic bending within the full ambient state space. We further relate extrinsic bending to variations in the unitary generator of motion along intrinsic geodesics. We present exact many-body geometric results for the transverse-field XY spin chain. The product structure of the ground state leads to an exact cancellation of the ambient tide, including its Berry-curvature enhancement, by extrinsic curvature contributions. At the zero-field Ising point, we obtain exact results at finite size and show that the shear source for anisotropy-directed motion is entirely extrinsic relative to the full many-body state-space. For the metric in the thermodynamic limit, the geodesic families exhibit repeated $A_2$ fold catastrophes inside the ferromagnetic phase. Our framework thus separates universal state-space effects from those of physical restrictions and exposes their consequences in a paradigmatic many-body system.

papers.title: Krylov meets Fock: Complementary lenses on quantum dynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum dynamics in Krylov space can be represented by a particle hopping on a chain whose sites are the Krylov basis vectors. The goal of this work is to extend this idea to the Fock basis, which in turn allows the description of a generic dynamics in terms of a more general, possibly higher-dimensional lattice. This construction has been dubbed the Fock state lattice (FSL), since its sites are identified with Fock states. To analyze the dynamics on the FSL we introduce various measures of the spread of a state, comparing them among themselves and with their Krylov counterparts. We apply our analysis to two models of light-matter interaction studied in quantum optics: the multi-mode Jaynes-Cummings and the Dicke models. We find that, whenever the FSL is not a chain, the corresponding dynamics provides insights complementary to the Krylov space analysis and, in some instances, greater analytical control. For example, we obtain analytical results for the FSL spread measures of the Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit and determine that their scaling in time detects the superradiant phase transition.

papers.title: Zero noise extrapolation of transport coefficients
papers.abstract: NISQ devices routinely estimate properties of the noiseless system from measurements at varying noise strengths $γ$. These zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) schemes fail to estimate transport coefficients of conserved quantities when the noise violates the associated conservation laws. We show how to extrapolate measurements in noisy, one-dimensional, non-integrable spin chains to obtain the spin transport coefficients governing linear response in the zero-noise limit. As the wavevector of the Fourier mode of a conserved quantity goes to zero, its decay rate vanishes. The coefficient of the leading momentum dependence defines a transport coefficient in the noiseless system, and an analogous effective coefficient in the noisy one. Naive ZNE implicitly assumes that this effective coefficient is analytic in $γ$ as $γ\to 0$. Our main result is that universal non-linear corrections to hydrodynamics can produce non-analytic dependence on $γ$. In particular, we argue that the effective spin diffusion coefficient of a dissipative Heisenberg chain and the effective subdiffusion coefficient of a dipole-conserving fracton approach their noiseless value as $γ^{1/2}$. We benchmark these analytical predictions numerically.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论为主，辅以数值验证；依据为解析论证加数值基准。；研究对象：一维非可积自旋链；耗散 Heisenberg 链与偶极守恒 fracton 体系。

english_guide.evidence: Analytical argument that the decay rate of a conserved Fourier mode vanishes as wavevector goes to zero; the leading momentum coefficient defines transport coefficients; effective spin diffusion and subdiffusion coefficients scale as γ^{1/2}; numerical benchmarks.
english_guide.method: Hydrodynamic analysis of noisy one-dimensional non-integrable spin chains, defining effective transport coefficients, with numerical benchmarking.
english_guide.novelty: Authors state that universal non-linear corrections to hydrodynamics can produce non-analytic dependence on γ, invalidating analyticity assumptions of naive ZNE.
english_guide.limitations: Restricted to one-dimensional non-integrable spin chains and the two named systems; no specific numbers, noise-model details, or experimental conditions given.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称主要结果是普适非线性流体力学修正可导致对 γ 的非解析依赖，使朴素 ZNE 的解析性假设失效。

papers.title: Noise-Induced Topology in Chiral Quantum Walks
papers.abstract: Noise typically destroys quantum coherence and washes out transport phenomena that rely on interference. Chiral quantum walks are a case in point: a particle hopping on a lattice threaded by a magnetic flux can spread asymmetrically due to interference between paths, an asymmetry that noise is expected to erase. Remarkably, we find that the most ubiquitous noise -- random fluctuations of on-site energies (dephasing) -- instead renders this asymmetry topologically robust. The density profile develops a skewness that grows in time while its center stays fixed, and in a finite chain the late-time relaxation modes pile up at one edge: a skin effect lacking the drift of conventional non-Hermitian skin effects. With multiple sites per unit cell, the dephasing strength alone can cause a topological phase transition, reversing the asymmetry. On a flux ladder with noisy rung hopping, the noise causes a drift of rung coherences, a quantum ratchet with no classical counterpart. Underlying these effects, the noise-averaged dynamics is an interacting (generically non-integrable) Lindbladian that remains analytically tractable. The modes governing late-time relaxation are bound states of the noise-induced interaction and form a band with a point gap, absent both without noise and under postselection, whose winding number fixes the direction of the asymmetry. These effects are within reach of several experimental platforms, including synthetic lattices, superconducting qubits, and optical lattices.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论；基于噪声平均Lindbladian的解析研究；研究对象：手性量子行走（chiral quantum walks），含磁通格点、通量梯子（flux ladder）及多格点原胞体系
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 退相位噪声（dephasing）非但不破坏手性量子行走的输运不对称性，反而使其获得拓扑鲁棒性，并可仅凭噪声强度驱动拓扑相变、反转不对称方向。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：噪声通常被认为会洗掉依赖干涉的手性输运不对称性，本文追问退相位噪声对该不对称性的实际作用及其机制。
证据与比较：密度分布偏度随时间增长而中心不动；有限链中晚期弛豫模式堆积于一侧边缘，形成无漂移的趋肤效应；多格点原胞下仅退相位强度即可触发拓扑相变并反转不对称；通量梯子上噪声引起梯级相干漂移。
papers.method_zh: 将噪声平均动力学表述为相互作用、一般不可积的Lindbladian并进行解析处理，考察晚期弛豫模式构成的能带、点隙与绕数。

english_guide.question: Does the most ubiquitous noise, random on-site energy fluctuations (dephasing), erase the interference-based asymmetric spreading of chiral quantum walks, or can it instead stabilize it topologically?
english_guide.evidence: Density profiles develop growing skewness with fixed center; finite chains show edge-piled late-time relaxation modes, a skin effect lacking conventional non-Hermitian drift; multiple sites per unit cell yield a dephasing-driven topological transition; a flux ladder with noisy rung hopping shows drifting rung coherences, a quantum ratchet.

english_guide.limitations: Abstract does not specify parameter regimes, finite-size or noise-strength ranges; experimental platforms (synthetic lattices, superconducting qubits, optical lattices) are only noted as within reach, with no data.

papers.title: Toward a Quantum Information Foundation for Neutron Scattering
papers.abstract: Neutron scattering is a central probe of quantum materials, yet what quantum information can, in principle, be extracted from a scattering experiment remains unclear. Here we formulate neutron scattering as a quantum measurement, with the scattering amplitudes acting as Kraus operators on the material state. This provides a unified description of conventional intensity, coherent scattering, interferometric measurements, and entanglement witnesses, including those based on quantum Fisher information. We then ask how far this connection can be extended to nonlinear properties of a quantum state. For two independently prepared samples, we derive the general structure of probe-mediated measurement probabilities and show that, for spin-projection-conserving dynamics, low-order scattering cannot resolve certain many-body coherences required to determine purity. Conversely, an idealized single-spin protocol shows how probe-mediated exchange can access purity when the appropriate two-copy operation is realized. Our results establish a quantum-information description of neutron scattering and delineate the information accessible through conventional and interferometric measurements.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论；基于量子测量与Kraus算符形式化推导；研究对象：中子散射实验及被探测的量子材料态
